# K-ALG-003：前缀缓存：计算等价类、Radix 与淘汰收益

可复用前缀是能产生等价中间状态的一组输入和执行条件；字符串相同只是其中一个投影。

## 为什么历史 KV 可以复用

因果模型中，位置 t 的各层状态只依赖可见前缀以及模型参数、位置规则和外部条件。当这些依赖保持一致，两个请求在分叉前的状态可以共用。此结论来自计算图：若某个依赖进入了状态生成，却没有进入缓存身份，命中就可能跨越不同计算。

因此身份一般需要模型及权重版本、规范化后的 token 序列、位置编码配置、影响状态的 adapter、多模态特征身份，以及隔离命名空间。sampling temperature 通常影响之后如何选 token，不影响已给定前缀的前向状态；但已采样出的 token 已经属于前缀。不要把所有配置都盲目混入 key，也不要漏掉真正参与前向的输入。

把一个明确的前向条件记为 η，已知输入 token 序列记为 x[0:n)。逻辑缓存对象是该条件下完成到位置 p 的状态 S(η,x[0:p))，不是一个 token 字符串或一个地址。复用要求能够还原同一后续计算所需的状态：普通因果 Attention 是每层有效 K/V，混合模型还可能需要窗口、递归状态等。请求输出是实际可继续的位置 p、对应的状态句柄与就绪关系，以及尚需处理的输入 x[p:n)。空缓存返回 p=0；空输入是否允许由任务定义，生成任务若没有任何输入，应先提供合法起始输入，不能从空 KV 自动生成一个已知末行。

模型函数上的等价不自动成为浮点逐位相同。状态格式、量化尺度、位置规则或允许的误差契约改变后，需要重验复用边界；同一前缀由不同数据流生成时也可能有舍入差异。若前向中存在影响状态的随机操作，还需保存相应身份/状态或禁用这种复用。缓存 salt 只提供一个隔离命名空间；是否授权共享、目录暴露与时序泄露的治理仍由系统语义决定。

## 块哈希和 Radix 是两种索引结构

链式块哈希使当前块身份依赖父块身份、当前 token 和额外条件。相同 token 块出现在不同上下文中，不会被误认为相同状态。Radix 树把共享 token 路径压缩为边，前缀匹配可能在边内结束，此时需要拆分节点，节点下挂物理状态与引用关系。树负责发现最长共享路径，物理池负责保存内容，两者不必一一对应一个分配对象。

例如 A 的前缀是 a,b,c,d，B 是 a,b,c,e。共享可到 c；物理块大小若为 4，则逻辑前缀命中长度 3 与可直接共享整块数量 0 是不同结果。支持尾块复制可保留部分收益，否则重算这段可能比小块管理更划算。不能把逻辑最长匹配直接当作内核可跳过的 token 数。

下面选“仅完整页进入缓存目录、固定页长 P、同一模型状态的所有必要层均完成后才发布”作为具体算法。它便于把命中、物理共享与追加分开证明；不要求其他引擎使用同样的块大小或结构。第 j 页的精确身份包含 η、页边界、父前缀身份及 x[jP:(j+1)P)。可以递推计算桶号 hⱼ=H(域标签, hⱼ₋₁, 本页 token, 额外条件)，根桶号包含 η。仅将本页 token 做哈希会把不同历史中的同一段混在一起。

哈希只缩小候选集合。本例保存可核对的完整身份，查询时核对 η、完整父身份与本页内容；父身份可以由共享的父结点表示，无须给每页复制一份完整 prompt。父哈希碰撞不能再用“父哈希相同”证明父身份相同。选用概率性身份时应明确其碰撞契约，不能将任意有限哈希写成无碰撞定理。序列化还须表达类型、长度与边界，否则不同字段连接可能先于哈希就变成同一字节串。索引元数据自身也需计容量和回收；保留子结点时仍须保留其身份依赖，不等于必须永久保留所有历史请求的 token 副本。

Radix 可以按 token 串而非整页寻找最长匹配。其边内分叉算法为：从根出发，与下一条边标签逐 token 比较；完整匹配则下行；在第 k 个元素处分歧则建立长度 k 的公共边，将旧剩余后缀与新后缀挂到公共结点下；若查询在边内结束，可返回该偏移，不一定要立即改变树。拆边只重排索引与状态切片的描述；物理页是否可共享仍由页边界、有效范围与所有权决定。插入尚未完成的 token 路径不能同时发布对应 K/V 已就绪。SGLang 固定论文的实例采用单 token 页，本节的 P>1 完整页策略是另一种独立构造，不能归为该论文的同一物理实现。

## 命中长度是全状态一致的交点

有些层保留全历史，有些只保留窗口，有些保存递归状态。能恢复整个模型执行的位置，必须让所有需要的状态在该位置同时有效。某一层有 4k token KV 不代表模型可从 4k 继续，递归层可能只有 2k 处的检查点。分层命中长度的最小值仅在每层有效集合都是从零开始的连续前缀时成立；一般要取各类恢复位置集合的交集。

令每种状态允许恢复的位置集合为 Rᵍ，索引与真实状态就绪共同允许的位置为 I，则选择 p∈I∩⋂Rᵍ。例如完整 KV 支持 0…12，递归检查点在 {4,8,12}，所需窗口只覆盖允许从 {8,12} 恢复的位置，而外部状态当前仅到 8，真正的共同上界是 8；分别取“每层最大长度”再忽略位置集合会给出错误结论。普通完整页算法只在 0,P,2P,… 上查找，遇到第一个缺页就停止；本例不能跳过缺失的父页而使用更深的孤立页。

即使 n 个输入 token 的 KV 全部命中，开始生成仍可能缺少最后一个已知输入位置的 logits。只存 KV 的本例令可跳过上限为 n−1，再按 P 向下取整；例如 n=8、P=4 时最多直接跳过 4 个 token，最后一整页需要安全重算，不能假装已得到第一个新 token 的分布。n=9 则最多跳过 8。若任务只需恢复 KV 而不需生成，或另外保存了满足同一输出契约的末行 logits，可使用不同上限。重算区域必须私有或经过证明的写入隔离，不能覆盖仍被其他请求共享的命中页。调度如何区分已知 token 与已完成 KV 见[连续批处理](iteration-batching.md)。

## 从查询到发布的完整操作

下面保持缓存页内容不可变，区分三种拥有关系。C 表示目录为了未来命中而保留该页；A 表示当前请求的逻辑映射；R 表示已经提交的实际读取；构造中的新页另有 W 写入/暂存保留。请求结束只撤销 A，不自动撤销 C，也不会结束 R。目录命中资格与物理复用资格因此不同。页可分给下一内容的充分条件是 C=A=R=W=0。这里把分页章中的逻辑所有者进一步拆成缓存与请求，两者合计才是完整的逻辑拥有责任。

对目录、页池与请求快照采用同一主机协调关系：查询后保护命中、选择淘汰对象和取得新页之间不能留出可被另一分配者抢占的空隙。可以使用串行协调或其他能证明同样线性化效果的方法；不是只给每条请求各加一把锁就自动保护了共享页池。

```pseudocode
输入：请求身份、η、已知 x[0:n)、本轮合法输入额度 q上限、目录与页池
核对生成所需的非空输入，确定可跳过上限及各状态共同恢复资格
在目录/页池协调区内：
    从根按完整页查询；每一步核对完整身份、真实句柄代次和状态就绪
    在第一个缺失或其内容未就绪的位置前停止，得到所有已匹配完整页边界
    将匹配边界与各状态恢复集合求交，选择可跳过上限内最大的 p；无非零交点则 p←0
    为全部命中页增加本请求的 A，形成不可变的命中快照
    令 q←min(q上限,n−p)，按实际写入方案计算新页、输出及暂存资源
    先模拟足以满足本轮资源的合法淘汰与分配；不足则撤销本次 A，不提交计算
    原子撤下被选冷页的目录资格，再释放其 C；取得全部新页的 W
提交本轮计算前，为命中状态和描述取得 R，并建立输入就绪依赖
在私有写区计算 x[p:p+q)；未完成的长度和 token 身份不进入可命中目录
计算结束后，核对所有必要状态确实完成，并建立消费者可见的依赖
在协调区内复核请求身份、当前快照及取消资格：
    若仍可提交，发布新的请求状态，将 W 交接为请求 A
    只把新完成的完整页加入目录，并取得 C；未满尾页保持私有
    若同身份已有可用页，保留已有目录项；本请求可暂持自己的重复副本
    若已取消，不发布新状态；等所有可能的读写完成后放弃构造页
按实际最后使用释放 R；事务恰好一次地交接或释放 W
最终请求结束时撤销 A；仍有 C 或 R 的页继续保留
```

本轮 q 可以小于 n−p，只有已处理完全部已知输入时，末行才具备生成资格。命中避免的是其前缀的重算，新 suffix 仍需要读取这些前缀 K/V 做 Attention。若一个状态族或远端传输尚未就绪，不能仅因 token 路径存在而让它进入已完成长度。模型计算发生错误时保留旧快照；设备已接受的读写必须经过已声明的完成/排空关系后才能释放。主机源描述在复制完成前也应保持有效。

同时计算出相同前缀的请求可能产生两份物理副本。立即改写正在消费的页表去消除重复需要额外证明；本例让已有目录页继续负责未来命中，另一份副本随当前请求结束后回收。身份相同不意味着可以忽略正在使用的实际句柄。若选择在提交消费者前统一映射到同一页，应把重映射、引用交接和旧副本释放写成另一个完成的事务。

## 淘汰、再次命中与最后读者

本例的缓存目录形成前缀依赖树，采用叶优先淘汰：只选择没有缓存子结点、A=R=W=0 的缓存叶；先撤销目录可发现性，再释放 C，将满足全零条件的页交给分配者。删除叶可能让其父结点成为新的候选。访问时间、估计收益或其他策略决定候选排序，但不能越过资格条件。持续没有可回收叶时应等待、减少本轮工作、重算/转移其他状态或拒绝，不保证 LRU 总能找到足够空间。

只有 R>0 的冷页，即使请求已取消，也不能当作可立即增加容量的淘汰对象。本例保留其目录直到可回收；另一设计可以提前撤目录、把物理页放入等待回收集合，但必须把“已从索引删除”与“可用容量已增加”分开。远端目录还需要证明位置/版本、传输结果和目标页就绪；目录曾经命中不保证后来仍持有同一内容。

取 P=4、每 token 全层 KV 为 τ=128 KiB、页组大小 512 KiB，物理池只有 5 页，即预留 2.5 MiB。以下小写字母代表不同 token ID，所有请求前向条件一致，仅完整页可缓存：

| e1 | B 输入 abcdefghx，命中 8 个 token，私有页 2 保存 x；读者 B0 使用三页 | B 取消后 A=0，但 0、1、2 均因 B0 的 R 存活；0、1 还由 C 保留 |
| e2 | C 输入 abcdwxyzz，命中页 0，页 3 保存完成的 wxyz 并入目录，页 4 是私有 z | 所有 5 页存活；请求 C 保护 0、3、4 |
| e3 | D 输入 QRSTU，需要两个私有页，当前没有可回收页 | 页 1 虽是冷叶，但 B0 未结束；页 3 仍被 C 拥有，不能将“缓存可淘汰”当作两页可用 |
| e4 | B0 真正完成，尾页 2 释放；从目录淘汰冷叶 efgh，撤销页 1 的 C | 现在 1、2 两页可分给 D；页 0 仍是 C 所需前缀，不能为了淘汰父页破坏活分支 |
| e5 | D 完成 QRST 的新页后可缓存；再次查询 abcdefghx | 只能命中 abcd，即 4 个 token；旧 efgh 身份不能命中已复用的页 1 |

## 缓存价值与路由

命中收益近似为避免的重算时间减去索引、传输和映射成本。淘汰排序可以估计再访问概率×重算成本/驻留字节，并叠加引用保护。仅按 token 命中率会高估短且便宜前缀，忽视很长但少见的昂贵前缀。前缀亲和路由能提高局部命中，但可能把热门前缀集中到排队最严重的实例；路由代价应比较额外排队和节省的计算。

## 状态与容量的共同约束

设每页容纳 B 个 token；对不共享、全历史驻留的单个状态族，已分配范围 a 需要 ⌈a/B⌉ 页。若从 c 扩展到 c+q+r，其中 q 是本次工作、r 是额外预留，则新增页数为 max(0,⌈(c+q+r)/B⌉−已持有页数)。多个层组、窗口、共享页与压缩残余必须分别计账，不能直接把逻辑页数相加当作唯一物理占用。

例如 B=16、当前 c=31 且持有 2 页，本轮 q=2、r=0 时需再分配 1 页；若再预留 r=16，则需要再分配 2 页。预留增加未来推进余量，也挤占其他请求的容量。完整序列准入与按步分配是不同轴：前者保守地限制过度准入，后者灵活但可能在未来遇到不足。

## 命中与执行的交接

```pseudocode
匹配与当前模型、位置和表示一致的可恢复前缀
确认所需状态族都可恢复；外部尚未到达的数据保持不可消费状态
按本轮工作和预留量计算实际新增容量，保护命中页并建立新页归属
执行或传输完成后发布有效状态；失败时撤销本次未兑现的承诺
请求结束后撤销逻辑持有，等最后消费者结束再决定保留为缓存或复用存储
```

[已核对的块管理实例](../sources/S-VLLM-KV.md) 只复用完整缓存块，并为取得 logits 保留重新计算末尾的机会。若长度 32 的输入全部 KV 已缓存、页长 16，而命中范围受“最多 31 个 token 且完整块”限制，最多复用 16 个，重算可能是 16 个 token，不能固定计为 1。其他设计可以保存 logits 或允许不同恢复粒度，但会改变驻留与身份管理。

## 比较连续、分页和分层驻留

连续地址简化读取，但扩展与碎片可能增加搬运或预留；分页以索引换细粒度容量管理；虚拟映射可以保持地址连续而改变物理绑定；卸载还需目标预留、传输和可见性确认。这些表示都要解释引用、生存期和失败恢复，见[内存分配器](../system-semantics/memory-allocators.md)与[多级驻留](../algorithms/tiered-residency.md)。

区分容量问题与可用性问题，可保持逻辑输入相同，分别延迟外部传输、增加预留、造成跨页扩展或保留在途引用，记录每一状态族的已占、已预留、可消费与可回收量。调用释放函数不等于已经允许覆盖仍被设备或传输读取的存储。

## 等价、粒度与可恢复性

相同 token 前缀只有在模型、adapter、位置与其他影响计算的条件一致时才可能复用。树按公共 token 片段共享路径；固定块链用前驱身份和当前块标识前缀；直接重算不保留索引状态。三种方案都合法，取舍取决于重用长度与频率、查找/分叉成本、驻留和回收粒度。

[已核对的 Radix 实例](../sources/S-SGLANG-CODE.md) 在 token 之外使用命名空间区分不能共享的条目，匹配可能切分边以显式表示边界，活跃路径通过引用保护退出可淘汰集合。树边的逻辑 token 粒度与物理页粒度可以不同；不能用最长匹配长度直接代替所有状态族的共同恢复点。

## 一次复用与回收

```pseudocode
以模型相关身份和 token 前缀定位候选缓存
核对可恢复范围、表示与数据可用性，保护本次将消费的路径和状态
计算未命中部分，在合法完成点发布可共享的新状态
请求退出时撤销其持有；仍有消费者的节点继续受保护
需要容量时，按所选策略淘汰没有活动依赖的内容，并同步撤销索引身份
```

这个语义流程不要求树或哈希表。树可从未保护叶子逐步回收，共享祖先仍受保护；块池也需在复用存储前使旧缓存身份失效。远端目录命中、字节到达和执行器可消费是不同阶段，见[分布式 KV](../system-semantics/distributed-kv-store.md)。

## 收益与反例

复用收益来自省下的计算与读取，代价包括查找、身份检查、分叉/插入、保留容量与可能的传输。如果公共前缀短、重用很少或保存它会挤掉更有价值的状态，直接重算可能更合适；长且反复使用的前缀则可能抵偿索引和驻留成本。高命中率本身不说明省了多少时间。

在相同重用轨迹上比较树、块链和不缓存，记录实际跳过的工作与完整时间。构造 token 相同但 adapter 或命名空间不同的输入，应禁止错误共享；一个请求结束、另一个仍读取公共前缀时，公共状态应继续受保护。将传输延迟与目录旧记录分别注入，可以区分索引命中和恢复失败。

# K-FW-006：Attention 执行：数学语义、分块归约、低精度与硬件数据流

Attention 的设计从数学语义进入数据流：每个 query 对哪些 key 可见、Q/K/V 的几何、K/V 的状态表示，以及准备与执行怎样分段，共同定义输入与依赖。分块、工作划分、异步和低精度分别改变并行度、读取、驻留与误差；本章从算法推到成本和可否定的实验预测，性能排名只对确定的运行点成立。

## 问题、不变量与设计轴

问题：引擎持有的是逻辑状态——每个请求的绝对位置、有效长度、页表或偏移、head 映射、量化尺度——而 kernel 接受的是张量、索引数组与标志。要回答的是：怎样把逻辑状态变成 kernel 输入，每次调用付出哪些工作，哪些工作能在多次调用间摊销，换一个 kernel 时什么必须原样保持。

任何解都要满足的不变量：每个 query 行实际读取的 key 集合恰好等于模型定义的集合，包括因果对齐、窗口、填充与自定义规则，多读或少读都是另一个函数；query 长度与 KV 长度、Hq 与 Hkv 的映射、QK 维与 VO 维各自独立表达，不能靠相等假设省略；每个逻辑位置的 K、V 与量化尺度一致，同一槽位的并发更新具有明确的次序或合并语义，不能让无序覆盖改变状态；scale、softmax 稳定化、累加精度与分区合并在约定容差内保持同一函数；拆开计算的 key 子集互不重叠且并集完整。

成本项：转换（gather、转置、dtype 变换、mask 打包）、准备（消费 metadata、划分工作、选择实现）、执行（kernel 本身、输出与统计量的分配、事后缩放）、驻留（workspace、metadata 缓冲、布局副本）、同步（host 读取设备侧长度、图外提交）。每一项都要问它在哪个频率上发生：每任务、每模型加载、每形状、每层、每 batch 还是每 decode 步。

设计轴与已有方案所在的点：状态表示——稠密 padded、ragged 偏移、分页索引，padded 简单且图友好但付无效行，分页用间接寻址换容量；准备与执行的边界——每次调用全部重算、按几何缓存计划、把工作划分写成固定缓冲中的数据，摊销边界本身是设计变量；布局——页内 token 优先或 head 优先，K/V 合并或分离，生产者按消费者布局写出、消费前转换或 kernel 直接读生产者布局；可见性表达——布尔 mask、结构参数（因果、窗口）、块稀疏索引，结构参数最省也最弱；分区与合并——不拆，或沿 KV 拆再合并统计量。轴上未列点同样合法；下面各节按轴展开已知点的前提与代价。

## 先写出共同函数

对一个请求和一个 query head，设 Q∈ℝ^{L×dₖ}、K∈ℝ^{S×dₖ}、V∈ℝ^{S×dᵥ}，输出 O∈ℝ^{L×dᵥ}。L 与 S 不必相等，dₖ 与 dᵥ 也不必相等。给定缩放 a（通常为 1/√dₖ）、位置偏置 bᵢⱼ 和合法 key 集合 Aᵢ，定义 zᵢⱼ=a·QᵢKⱼᵀ+bᵢⱼ，pᵢⱼ=exp(zᵢⱼ)/Σ_{k∈Aᵢ}exp(zᵢₖ)，Oᵢ=Σ_{j∈Aᵢ}pᵢⱼVⱼ。不可见位置不进入分母。这里讨论推理且不施加 dropout；若模型需要随机丢弃，概率与随机流是另一个明确契约。

分组查询还需要一个 query head 到 KV head 的映射 h。常见均匀分组令每 Hq/Hkv 个 query heads 共享一组 K/V；整除是这种映射的前提，不是所有可能 head 映射的数学必然。物理页号、压缩布局和稀疏索引只在保持相同 Aᵢ、h 和内容时属于等价表示。删除合法 key 则改变模型函数。

问题出现于中间矩阵：直接计算会生成 L×S 个分数和概率，而最终只需要 L×dᵥ 个输出。长历史放大临时驻留与重复读写；短 query 又使按 query 切分的并行度不足。可用的片上存储、数据重用与并行任务数共同决定算法组织，不能只按 FLOPs 判断。

实现选择可以放在运行时分派、编译/调优或显式计划中；一条实现也可以同时采用几种方式。框架算子提供统一语义并根据条件分派，调用方仍需核对可见性和实际路径；融合实现控制数据流但可能要求特定几何；准备/执行分段可摊销 metadata 工作，也引入计划有效性与驻留成本。它们是可组合的设计轴，不能仅由库名推断成本。框架语义实例见 [S-SDPA](../sources/S-SDPA.md)。

## 从零实现时的算法骨架

下面给出一种精确稠密 Attention 的分块表达，不排除其他等价算法。先固定合法集合与有限的可见分数；输入含 NaN 或正无穷时要另行约定处理。为使空行行为可检查，本节示例规定无合法 key 的行输出零并标记为空；这是本例的契约，不能据此推断任意接口都采用它。

```pseudocode
输入：Q、K、V，缩放 a，位置偏置，合法集合 A，每块大小 Br、Bc
对每个 query 块，载入 Q；逐行初始化最大值 m←−∞、质量 ℓ←0、加权和 U←0
    对每个 K/V 块，按逻辑位置或页表载入所需 K、V
        计算 z←a·QKᵀ＋偏置，仅保留 A 中的位置
        对本块至少有一个合法 key 的行：
            m新←max(m，本块合法 z 的最大值)
            r←exp(m−m新)；首次非空块时 r←0
            P←exp(z−m新)，非法位置的 P←0
            U←r·U＋PV；ℓ←r·ℓ＋每行 P 的和；m←m新
        本块没有合法 key 的行保持原状态
    ℓ>0 的行输出 O←U/ℓ、LSE←m＋ln ℓ
    ℓ=0 的行输出零并标记为空，LSE←−∞
```

不变量是：处理完任意一组 key 后，m 是这组合法分数的最大值，ℓ=Σexp(z−m)，U=Σexp(z−m)V。新块改变 m 时，旧 ℓ 与 U 同乘 exp(m旧−m新)，于是旧贡献与新贡献仍处于同一尺度。最后 U/ℓ 恢复整体 softmax。只保存分块中间量，避免将 L×S 矩阵写入设备主存；浮点计算仍受归约顺序和精度影响，数学等价不表示逐位相同。

按单个 query head、Q 在外层并忽略 cache 命中，K/V 重读字节约为 ⌈L/Br⌉·S·(dₖ+dᵥ)·b，b 是输入元素字节数；另计 Q 读取、输出写回、索引和统计量。GQA 跨 head 复用需要另建共享映射，不能自动把这个单 head 公式乘 Hkv。Br 增大可减少遍历次数，却增加 Q、FP32 U、分数片段与多级缓冲的片上需求，进而影响驻留任务数或引发 spill。将 K/V 置于外层则改变哪些状态需要反复写回；循环顺序是存储和并行度的交换。

decode 的 L 很小时，可以把合法 K/V 切成互不重叠的 C 个分区；每区使用同一算法，保留归一化输出和 LSE，再按下一节的合并关系得到最终输出。C 增大会增加可调度任务，也增加 C·L·dᵥ 量级的部分输出与统计量、合并读取和提交成本。C=1 是合法候选；分区数应由真实并行度与完整调用成本决定。按长度估计任务成本并做最长任务优先分配，是 [FlashInfer 论文](../sources/S-FLASHINFERPAPER.md) Algorithm 1 的一个实例，其固定工作区上界依赖该算法的具体划分规则，不能外推到任意切分。

矩阵乘、softmax 与搬运之间还可建立流水。只有硬件允许相关指令异步推进、且缓冲生命周期满足依赖时，重叠才能实现；更深流水会延长分数与部分输出的存活时间。寄存器、共享存储和驻留任务数可能使收益反转，见 [GPU 流水](../hardware/gpu-kernel-pipelines.md) 与 [S-FLASHATTENTION3](../sources/S-FLASHATTENTION3.md)。

分页使逻辑 K/V 块经页表定位到物理块，并要求处理页边界和最后一页的有效长度；物理页大小与计算 tile 不必相同。分页控制分配碎片并支持共享，代价包含索引、非连续事务及可能降低的向量化效率。[PagedAttention](../sources/S-PAGED.md) §7.1 在图 18 所示设置与 FasterTransformer 基线的比较中报告 kernel 额外开销；该数字只属于那个比较。共享前缀可通过读取复用或独立计算后合并复用，不保证无需额外 metadata 或合并缓冲。

[FlashAttention](../sources/S-FLASH.md) 定理 2 在其二级存储模型、N×d 输入与 d≤M≤Nd 条件下给出 Θ(N²d²/M) 次元素级 IO；M 是可容纳的标量元素数，换成字节要统一元素精度。其命题 3 排除在整个 M 区间上一致达到更低阶 IO 的算法，没有证明每个固定 M 上的参数化下界，更没有证明某个现成 kernel 对任意硬件最优。

## FlashAttention-1、2、3 分别解决什么问题

它们计算相同的 Attention 数学函数，但针对不同的成本改写数据流。下面按前向推理展开；数学等价不保证不同有限精度实现逐位一致，FP8还引入额外量化误差。

## 转换成本与可复算反例

设一层 K/V 各有 L=8,192、Hkv=8、d=128、FP16，合计 2×8,192×8×128×2=32 MiB。若每次调用先完整 gather 到连续布局，需要读取旧布局并写入新布局，单是转换至少产生约 64 MiB 有效字节，之后 attention 还会读取新缓冲。更快的连续 kernel 只有在抵消这些转换、额外驻留与同步后才构成收益。

独立小例中，对同一 query 设两个 logits 都为 0，V 分别为 0、2，则整体输出为 1。各分区输出为 0 和 2、LSE 同为 0，合并得 1；若第二分区同时包含第一个位置，错误合并会重复计数，得到 2/3。对 Q 长 2、K 长 5 的因果输入，再显式验证两行可见集合，而不只比较输出 shape。

接入测试应覆盖 GQA 的 head 映射、QK 与 VO 维度差异、非整页、窗口边界、prefix/suffix 不重叠、无可见 key、位置偏置和 quantization scale。对同一逻辑状态依次记录转换、准备、kernel、合并和输出路由的耗时/内存，并用独立稠密数学参考验证。长历史、低 batch 时分区可能增加并行度；短历史或转换占主导时，简单路径可能更快。选择应由接口交集与完整执行成本决定。

## 条件化成本：字节、计算、准备与驻留

设 D=d_out、K=d_in，每组元数据合计 m 字节。本节逐行 INT4 布局的精确码容量为：

B_code=D·ceil(K/2)，B_meta=D·ceil(K/G)·m，B_weight=B_code+B_meta+B_align。

更一般的连续 b-bit 位流才可使用 ceil(DKb/8)；逐行从新字节开始的布局应使用 D·ceil(Kb/8)。例如 D=3、K=3 的 INT4 码占 6 字节，不能用整张量连续位流的 5 字节估计本版布局。有效位宽为 8B_weight/(DK)，仅对 DK>0 定义。

对 4,096×4,096、4 bit、G=128、m=4，码为 8,388,608 字节，元数据为 524,288 字节，总计 8,912,896 字节，即 8.5 MiB、4.25 bit/weight；元数据是码字节的 6.25%。m=4 是成本设定，不声明本例对称格式必须存放零点。对齐、长度表、版本、重打包副本和工作区另计。

若 M 行激活的一次前向只读取每个权重和元数据一次，忽略尾组、激活与输出，权重读取口径的算术强度约为 16M/(b+8m/G) FLOP/字节。M=1、b=4、G=128、m=4 时约为 3.76；它不是完整设备算术强度，更不是设备事务或实际带宽。

完整解包到 FP32 时，上述压缩权重另产生 64 MiB 高精度副本。若每轮都写出再读取该副本，至少新增该副本的写读交通；容量与带宽收益可能被抵消。tile 内解包避免完整物化，却可能重复提取码和读取参数。需要比较移位、符号扩展、尺度乘法、类型转换和后续复用，不能从压缩比直接推算时间。

WMMA 算例的两个 FP16 输入 tile 合计 1,024 字节，FP32 输出暂存为 1,024 字节。accumulator 有 256 个 FP32 值，按 32 lane 平均为每线程 8 个累加值；实际寄存器还包括 fragment 输入、地址和临时量。输入单缓冲与独立输出暂存合计 2 KiB 共享容量，双缓冲另加 1 KiB 输入空间。

对 J=ceil(K/16)，仅按逻辑有效载荷计，输入暂存的共享写和 fragment 读取合计约 2,048J 字节，输出写回再普通读取为 2,048 字节；这些不是 bank 事务或 HBM 字节。本例保守同步组织有每阶段发布、每阶段读完及一次输出发布，共 2J+1 个 warp barrier。能否合并某些边界必须依据新的完成证明，不能从成本账直接删同步。

当 M=1 直接使用 16 行 tile，有效行利用率仅为 1/16；K 非整除还浪费末段乘加。可比较 scalar/GEMV、其他合法 tile、跨请求合批或 split-K。大 prefill 对权重的多行复用更高，固定转换和装载开销更易摊薄，但计算吞吐和驻留也更可能成为限制。

按组整数归约时，K=4,096、G=128 有 32 组。若 16×16 输出 tile 同时保留每组 FP32 部分和，仅它们就需 256×32×4=32 KiB。逐组缩放后累加可缩短生存期，但改变指令组织和浮点顺序；跨线程或跨 CTA 分组还增加部分和写读、通信和合并同步。

准备包括校准、量化、打包、布局转换、JIT 与图捕获。一次准备为 C_prep、每次节省 Δt、实际复用 R 次，只有 RΔt>C_prep 才可能在该边界内收回；形状未命中和重新打包另计。峰值驻留分别相加：packed 权重、尺度、同时存活的解包片段、高精度副本、工作区和图缓冲，不能因文件为 4 bit 就把运行时驻留按 4 bit 计算。

通信按实际物理副本计。尺度随权重复制到多个 rank，就有多份容量及传输；跨分片组还需保留逻辑组身份或生成新制品。动态激活尺度若依赖跨 rank 统计，需要归约及其完成同步。共享 HBM、执行单元或网络的阶段不能同时领取各自的理想重叠收益，应按依赖图和竞争资源估计关键路径。

| 条件变化 | 保留的关系 | 调整对象与成本 | 放弃或改选条件 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 小 batch decode，权重读取主导 | 压缩可减少候选读取字节 | 比较 tile 内解包、参数访问、启动、实际 dispatch | 新增转换和同步超过读取节省时保留较高精度路径 |
| 大 prefill，计算主导 | 同一权重可服务更多行 | 比较低位矩阵路径、转换后矩阵乘和成熟高精度 kernel | 低位路径不能有效使用计算单元时改选 |
| G 变小 | 更细网格可能减少近似误差 | 重建码与参数，增加组数、元数据和部分和成本 | 参数流量或工作区成为主项时增大组或改布局 |
| scale 存储精度降低 | 码由实际保存尺度解释 | 先转换并冻结尺度，再编码和验证 | 尺度不再有限且为正时拒绝配置 |
| b 从 4 改为 8 或其他值 | 量化数学和组身份可重新定义 | 更换完整位流版本、偏移与解码规则 | 本版 nibble 编解码直接拒绝，不沿用左移 4 位 |
| 目标架构改变 | 数值契约可保留 | 重核指令、布局、对齐、线程范围和驻留 | 无合法高效 kernel 时选成熟路径或重新打包 |

SmoothQuant 的 Wx=(WD)(D⁻¹x) 在实数上等价，要求 D 可逆且所有消费者补偿同一变换；量化后的误差仍需验证。FlashInfer 固定论文附录 F 的一条路径是 FP8 KV 存储、FP16 query/output 并执行反量化，不能据此声称整条 attention 均采用 FP8 矩阵算术。

## 诊断：竞争解释、独立参考与负对照

先用同一码和冻结参数做独立解码，再比较解量化后的高精度算子与目标 kernel，最后比较量化模型与原模型质量。三个边界分别定位表示/布局、执行数值和算法近似。

| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 区分实验 | 反证后的修正 |
|---|---|---|---|
| W4 比 W8 慢 | 解包、参数流量、fallback、小 M 启动或驻留下降 | 固定质量与 shape，改变 batch/组长，记录实际内核、local 交通、工作区和时间线 | 字节下降但耗时不降时查新增阶段和瓶颈位置 |
| shape 正确但数值错误 | nibble 顺序、符号扩展、组轴或尺度导出改变 | 用固定字节和独立解码，分别改变一组尺度或一个 nibble | 解码失败先修格式，再讨论量化质量 |
| 非默认位宽往返失败 | 用固定 nibble 协议解释其他 b | 尝试 b=8 的 [16,0]、[0,1]，要求编码和解码入口拒绝 | 若碰撞被接受，收紧契约或实现新版本完整位流 |
| 同一码的点积不同 | 分组尺度提出归约、累加顺序或转换精度不同 | 两组不同尺度，与逐元素解量化参考比较，注入单一 epilogue | 解码相同而归约错时修单位与应用位置 |
| WMMA 偶发错误 | 输入未发布、旧输入被覆盖、布局/ld 错 | 软件模型推迟发布和读完；设备上另做合法 load→store 交接并核验同步 | barrier 放在装载后仍错时移到消费前，重新证明作用域 |
| C_s 按行读取错误 | 集体写回未对普通读取可见、fragment 行列猜测或掩码错 | 先集体 store，再显式同步并按 C_s 下标比较；注入缺失输出发布 | 交接失败先修完成依赖和布局，不归因于量化误差 |

## TP 下的物理头副本

TP 先分配 query head，再从 μ 推导每个 rank 需要的 KV head。设 p 个 rank，Hq 能被 p 整除，每 rank 拥有 Hq/p 个连续 qhead，记集合 I_r。所需 KV 集合为 S_r={μ(h)|h∈I_r}。若采用本地复制而不远程读取，则每 rank 的 KV 主项按 |S_r| 计，全组按 Σ_r|S_r| 计；唯一模型状态仍只有 Hkv 个 head。

Hkv 能被 p 整除且组边界与 rank 对齐时，可以均匀分片。否则不能直接用 floor(Hkv/p) 或局部 qhead/KV 数量比代替原映射。

取 Hq=24、Hkv=6、p=4，原模型每 4 个连续 qhead 共用 KV，每 rank 分 6 个 qhead：

| rank | query heads | 必需逻辑 KV heads |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0…5 | {0,1} |
| 1 | 6…11 | {1,2} |
| 2 | 12…17 | {3,4} |
| 3 | 18…23 | {4,5} |

全组共 8 份物理 head 数据，容量为逻辑唯一状态的 8/6。rank 0 的局部两组分别有 4 和 2 个 qhead，局部 6/2=3 不是模型的 g=4。实现可使用显式 global-to-local 映射，或在支持的后端中按原组补齐 query、屏蔽填充输出并恢复顺序；后端仅接受均匀局部分组时，应改分片或并行度。

## 检查范围与剩余边界

随章文件 `tools/check_k_model_002_full.py` 是确定性、只读、离线的 Python 标准库检查。被测路径按 KV 组加载输入并在线合并，独立参考按正确 μ 展开成逐 qhead K/V，用 Decimal 整行 softmax 计算。覆盖 MHA、MQA、连续 GQA、显式不均匀映射，dK≠dV、偏置、逐 head 不等可见集合、空行、空历史、零 query、短尾块和不同分块。比较器拒绝非有限值；形状校验也实际拒绝误用 dV 宽度的历史 K 和新 K。

attention 的乘加计数发生在实际 QK/PV 标量循环中，与独立按可见项和通道枚举的参考及按 P_h 求和的公式核对。逻辑加载次数按组内可见集合并集核算，它计一对 K/V 向量的加载事件，不是设备事务。四投影检查实际构造小矩阵、执行标量乘加计数，再与按 token/head/channel/hidden 轴独立枚举的参考和推导式比较；错误 Q/O 宽度进入同一矩阵计数路径并被拒绝。

512 MiB、TP16 字节和有效位宽部分是资源算术核算；TP 局部集合另与人工推导的全局映射参考比较。这些检查没有分配相应设备缓存，也没有测量容量峰值。分页量化迁移轨迹用于解释组合身份与发布条件，脚本不实现其真实码格式或异步协议。

脚本交由协调者执行，实际执行状态以本轮证据记录为准。它只验证小尺寸 CPU 标量数学与成本模型，不验证 FP16/BF16/FP8 舍入、GPU/Neuron kernel、片上 barrier、内存可见性、物理事务、collective、模型质量或知识使用效果。目标设备实验还需固定制品、shape、布局、dtype、mask、预热和计时边界，并记录准备、资源、spill、同步和完整时间线。

# K-MODEL-006：MLA：压缩状态、矩阵吸收与解耦 RoPE

MLA 用一份低维内容 latent 和独立的位置 key 表示历史。缓存容量减少来自表示，decode 流量收益还要求计算真正沿该表示完成；若每步展开全部历史 K/V，持久状态小仍可能伴随大量计算和临时读写。

## 函数、输入与充分状态

普通 MHA 每层、每 token 保存各 head 的 K/V，共约 2H d_h 个元素。MLA 让 H 个 head 共用内容 latent，各 head 用不同的上投影解释它，并非把普通 KV head 简单合并。它是模型结构，不能凭下面的线性等式把任意已有 MHA checkpoint 无损改成 MLA。

采用列向量记法。h_t∈ℝ^d 是一层 attention 输入，H 是 query head 数，d_h 是内容 key 和 value 的每头维度，d_c 是 KV latent 宽度，d_q 是 query latent 宽度，d_R 是解耦位置宽度，L 是层数。本文采用来源公式中内容 K/V 同宽的情形；不同 value 宽度须分别改写投影和成本。各宽度为正整数，成对旋转要求 d_R 为偶数。MLA 的理想压缩要求 d_c+d_R 小于所比较缓存的每 token 宽度，但这不是吸收等式成立的条件，也不要求 d_c>d_h。

参数维度为 W_DKV∈ℝ^(d_c×d)、W_DQ∈ℝ^(d_q×d)、W_UK,i 和 W_UV,i∈ℝ^(d_h×d_c)、W_UQ,i∈ℝ^(d_h×d_q)、W_QR,i∈ℝ^(d_R×d_q)、W_KR∈ℝ^(d_R×d)，以及 W_O∈ℝ^(d×Hd_h)。W_O,i 是 W_O 对应 head i 的 d×d_h 列块。定义：

z_t = W_DKV h_t，s_t = Φ_KV(z_t)；
c_t = Φ_Q(W_DQ h_t)；
k^C_(t,i) = W_UK,i s_t，v^C_(t,i) = W_UV,i s_t；
q^C_(t,i) = W_UQ,i c_t；
k^R_t = R_(ρ(t)) W_KR h_t，q^R_(t,i) = R_(ρ(t)) W_QR,i c_t。

R_p 是制品指定的位置变换，ρ(t) 是模型坐标，不能由物理页号或 batch 行号代替。Φ_KV、Φ_Q 包括实际 latent 后的归一化与宽度缩放；简化论文图中的恒等映射只是一个特例。例如固定 gain g、宽度缩放 γ 与 ε>0 时，可有 Φ(z)=γ(g⊙z)/sqrt(Σ_a z_a²/width+ε)。实际参数和放置按制品核对。DeepSeek-V2 §3.1.2、DeepSeek-V3 v1 §4.2 都提到压缩 latent 后的额外 RMSNorm 和宽度瓶颈缩放，不能只为 KV 路径补 norm 而漏掉 query 路径。V2-Lite 不压缩 query，说明 query 压缩不是 MLA 的必要条件；这时直接按制品产生 q^C、q^R。

对 query t，A_t 是允许读取的逻辑 key 集合。有限输入域中：

e_(t,i,j) = α_model [q^C_(t,i)·k^C_(j,i) + q^R_(t,i)·k^R_j]，
a_(t,i,j) = exp(e_(t,i,j)) / Σ_(k∈A_t) exp(e_(t,i,k))，
o_(t,i) = Σ_(j∈A_t) a_(t,i,j) v^C_(j,i)，
u_t = Σ_i W_O,i o_(t,i)。

来源中的基础缩放 α_model=1/sqrt(d_h+d_R)。吸收后点积虽有 d_c 个内容通道，也不能改用 1/sqrt(d_c+d_R)。若 checkpoint 的长上下文策略还调整 attention 温度，应在 α_model 或所指定的分量中显式还原，不能重复施加。本文选择空 A_t 返

## 从逻辑 key 到物理地址

以 K、V 分开存储的分页 NHD 布局为例，页长 B 个 token，页表 table[l][b] 给出物理页号。逻辑位置 j 的逻辑页为 floor(j/B)，页内槽为 j mod B。K 地址为

baseK + (((table[l][floor(j/B)]·B+j mod B)·Hkv+h)·dₖ+x)·bK。

其中 x 是 K 通道号，bK 是每元素字节数。V 使用自己的 baseV、dᵥ 和 bV。head 优先、合并容器或量化布局需重新展开地址，不能沿用此式。物理页号不会进入 RoPE。

定位后还要验证该槽的逻辑标签、内容身份、代次和有效范围。页表回答地址，不证明地址中的字节已经完成、属于本次前缀或带有正确量化尺度。共享页

[EXCERPT extracted-character range 8000:12000]
56 KiB 内容读写，合计 512 KiB，尚不含 attention 读取、metadata 或 staging。P₂ 的额外分配为 512 KiB，不能只按其三个有效 token 估算。旧 P₁ 仍被前缀或在途读者持有时不能扣除；B 分叉还需自己的私有页。

同例 q=2、H=5，E=13；若 Hq=32，则每层 QK/PV 主乘加为 2·32·256·13=212,992 FLOP。这个量不包括投影，也不是时延预测。若 q=128、S=8192，单个无 head 复制的显式 mask 有 1,048,576 个元素，按每布尔 1 B 为 1 MiB，按 FP32 加性偏置为 4 MiB；广播能否保持视图而不物化要按实际路径核对。

串行路径可写 T=T准备+T复制/转换+T设备+T提交。存在重叠时，应沿生产者到消费者的依赖图取关键路径，并检查带宽等共享资源，不能把所有累计耗时相加，也不能只取最快 kernel 作为完整调用成本。

## 条件改变后保留什么

| 变化 | 可以保留的关系 | 需要调整或放弃的部分 |
|---|---|---|
| 只改变 padding、batch 顺序、物理页排列 | 输入与模型函数、逻辑位置、合法集合 | 重建执行行列和地址映射；检查 inactive 槽及归属 |
| 改变 chunk 划分 | 普通确定性因果模型的逻辑依赖 | staging、历史重读、准备次数及浮点归约；量化封组策略另作合同 |
| 窗口缩小 | 新窗口仍允许的状态内容 | 只在模型定义或质量合同允许时改变函数；等待读者结束再回收 |
| 窗口扩大 | 仍有合法副本的旧位置 | 已覆盖历史无法靠改长度恢复，应重算或取回副本 |
| RoPE 配对、频率、缩放或输入起点改变 | 仍完全不受影响的依赖 | 重新证明整个状态依赖；局部旋转公式不能代替多层证明 |
| raw K 与 rotated K 后端切换 | 已证明相同的未旋转内容与坐标 | 转换、舍入、表示标志和读写路径；量化往返通常不可逆 |
| 只改变布局或迁移设备 | 内容与位置语义 | 元数据、stride、head 排列、ready 依赖与峰值；含 scale 一起转换 |
| 模型、adapter、前缀或外部特征改变 | 无关请求的旧不可变对象 | 旧命中资格通常失效；同 token 数、同 shape 不足以复用 |
| 采用近似裁剪或重要 token 保留 | 被保留对象的身份与位置 | 原全 attention 函数已经改变，增加任务质量参考 |

短历史、小 q 时，显式小 mask 与简单路径可能比复杂计划便宜。长历史时，结构参数或融合 mask 更容易摊薄准备与驻留，但仅在能够准确表达全部可见性时使用。原生窗口降低有效对数并不保证执行 tile 和 DRAM 事务同比减少。未旋转 K 若被多步重复旋转可能不合算；旋转后缓存若带来迁移格式不兼容，也可能使整体成本反转。选择需要相同函数、输入、计时边界与容量约束。

## 竞争解释、负对照与检查边界

先检查具体可见关系，再比较输出。只检查可见对数、shape 或首 token 都可能漏错：两个集合可以大小相等但成员不同；首 token 可能尚未读取迁移或量化后的历史；纯 RoPE 的共同坐标平移还可能掩盖单一 padding 样例的问题。

| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 区分实验及反证后的修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 方形 prefill 正确，增量失败 | 非方形左上对齐；本块位置重置；旧 K 重复旋转 | 固定 H=5、q=2，先比较逐行逻辑集合，再比较原始与旋转后 K；集合错先修 mask，集合对再查位置数值 |
| padding 后结果变化 | 无效列进入分母；位置整体偏移；请求行路由错误 | 同一输入独立、左补齐、混批执行，改变 padding 内 V 为大有限 poison；另核对每个有效 token 的坐标和归属 |
| chunk 跨窗口时失败 | 提前覆盖；当前 key 重复；窗口端点错 | 执行 W=4、[5,8) 轨迹，记录每行位置标签与贡献次数；等分数参考为 3.5、4.5、5.5，分别注入覆盖和重复贡献 |
| 非整页命中后出错 | 尾页漏复制；有效长度扩到未填槽；共享页原地改写 | 新页以 poison 初始化，独立读取旧物理尾槽再复制；检查 A、B 和旧前缀的字节与后续输出，不能用全量重打包自动补好遗漏 |
| 迁移后标签正确但数值错 | raw/rotated 合同不匹配；尺度缺失；head/通道排列错误 | 固定逻辑输入，分别比较位置处理、解码后的 K/V 和逐行输出；若首次差异发生在解码前，修表示而不是放宽输出容差 |
| 只在取消或并发时错 | 早回收；迟到旧写；共享 workspace 覆盖 | 控制最后使用与完成顺序，复用槽后再放行旧事件；需要真实平台验证物理可见性，CPU 次序模型不足以证明设备协议 |
| kernel 更快但完整调用更慢 | mask/gather 准备；COW；同步；额外驻留降低并发 | 固定请求集分别计准备、转换、设备与提交，再放开容量准入；若优势仅来自更多并发，应归为容量收益 |

交付的 tools/check_k_sys_003_full.py 是确定性、离线、只读的 Python 标准库单层 CPU 模型。缓存路径实际维护分页槽或 ring、位置标签、raw/rotated K、无效列、共享非整页尾页的 COW 和物理重排；独立参考直接扫描逻辑序列，用上文相对旋转内积公式计算整行 softmax，不读取被测页表，也不调用被测旋转函数。

检查覆盖空新增、首行、非等长 Q/K、多种切分、非零与非单调位置坐标、左 padding、静态无效列、W=1、q>W、跨页、前缀分叉后继续和重排后继续。负对照实际改变左上对齐、mask 乘零、无效列参与、重复旋转、块内位置重置、槽号旋转、未来 key、重复自身以及提前 ring 覆盖，并要求独立参考或标签不变量拒绝。标签、坐标与身份破坏另有读取拒绝检查。

该模型不包含真实 Transformer 的投影学习、完整多层提交、采样恢复、量化误差、异步对象回收、GPU 原子与可见性或性能。普通高精度路径的分区等价，应在目标模型按约定容差继续验证；低位路径另需正确消费压缩历史的数值和质量实验。本轮 Python 脚本未执行，真实结果由协调者运行后保存。作者只进行了注明范围的 JavaScript 二进制双精度旋转恒等式、集合与字节算例检查；这些结果不构成 Python 检查通过或 GPU 实测。

## 对象身份与目录分开

缓存身份包含影响状态的模型/权重/adapter、规范化输入、位置规则、状态几何和表示策略。分块身份还要包含父前缀依赖，避免把不同上下文中的相同 token 块当成同一状态。目录保存对象到位置、副本与生命周期的映射，不应把远端地址或槽号直接用作内容身份。

目录可以按 token 前缀、块链或其他依赖索引查找；物理位置可能是 GPU、DRAM 或 SSD。一个节点上的状态完整，不意味着其他节点可以按相同布局直接读取；不同 TP/PP、分页和量化格式可能需要转换。混合状态模型还需要所有状态族在同一恢复位置可用。

[Mooncake v1](../sources/S-MOONCAKE.md) §3–5 给出共享 KV 池、链式块身份、传输组件和缓存感知调度的组织实例。它提供设计分支，不能替本项目证明任意缓存对象都可跨实例互换。

## 发布完整副本，再允许消费者使用

目的端先预留容量，将到达范围记为未提交；完成读取、转换及必要可见性后，才发布可消费副本。目录可以先登记正在构建的位置用于合并同类请求，但读者必须知道它尚未就绪，不能把它当作命中后可立即执行。

不可变前缀可有多个相同副本；可变尾块必须封闭版本或采用明确的更新协议。淘汰先阻止新引用，再等待在途读取与引用结束，最后释放物理位置。目录中的旧记录可能仍被迟到请求使用，因此位置代次与实际内容检查不能省略。

| 故障或竞争 | 可保持的语义 |
|---|---|
| 目录说存在但源已失效 | 将该位置视为不可读，选择其他副本或合法重算 |
| 一部分块到达后失败 | 保留未提交范围或撤销预留，不发布完整恢复点 |
| 同一前缀同时构建 | 可以合并等待，也可产生等价副本；容量与引用分别结算 |
| 模型版本改变 | 新旧身份分开，旧副本按旧读者生命周期回收 |
| 淘汰与读取交错 | 已取得访问权的读者仍受保护；新读者重新查找 |

缓存丢失通常可以通过重新计算恢复，但输出提交、请求随机状态或其他不可重建信息不能因为名称叫缓存就一并丢弃。控制平面重建目录，也不代表已恢复在途请求的业务状态。

## 本地命中、远端命中和重算

本地命中要计索引与映射，远端命中增加目录往返、源排队、传输、转换和目标容量等待；重算则支付剩余前缀执行。三者比较同一模型与输入语义，不能将任意文档单独计算的 KV 直接拼成新上下文。

设定对象 512 MiB，远端有效带宽 20 GiB/s，传输下界 25 ms，目录/排队/转换另需 15 ms。若重算为 30 ms，远端“命中”反而慢；若重算为 180 ms，则有潜在收益。[KV 压缩](../algorithms/kv-compression.md) 可进一步改变传输量，但需要编码身份、解码容量和质量条件。

负载维度也重要：到达率 λ、远端命中比例 h、每次实际读取 D，则平均网络需求约 λhD，副本复制、写入和重试另计。多个实例争用同一缓存节点/NIC 时，单次读取带宽不可直接沿用；目录查询本身也可能成为热点。

## 副本、热点和缓存预算

复制热门前缀可以分散读取和路由负载，却增加存储、后台网络与失效管理；逐出冷前缀又可能增加未来 prefill。可比较固定副本数、按读取压力增减、按预测收益放置和仅按请求拉取。缓存命中率、命中 token 数和真正避免的关键路径时间分别度量不同收益。

缓存池应保留服务状态与在途目的空间的余量。若所有容量都装满只读副本，新请求可能没有地方接收自己的状态。共享基础设施还需按模型、租户和权限命名空间定义可复用边界，不能让全局哈希替代隔离规则。

## 验证与选择反转

使用同一到达轨迹比较仅本地缓存、共享远端池和直接重算，扫描前缀重用距离、对象大小、冷热分布与源节点压力。验证旧目录、损坏范围、部分到达、源退出和重复请求的状态不变量，记录失效重算与资源释放。

长而昂贵、重复访问的前缀更有机会受益；短前缀、弱互联、高目录压力或热点排队可能更适合本地重算。分布式缓存的价值由这些条件和 SLO 共同决定，不能由池容量或命中率单独证明。

同一段文本在两个请求中出现，只能证明输入内容重复。它在某层产生的状态还取决于可见上文、位置规则和模型版本。非前缀复用的设计起点，是判定哪些依赖保持不变，以及允许用多少计算和质量损失处理其余依赖。

## 一段文本有多种可以缓存的对象

分词结果、独立文档 embedding、检索结果、decoder 的逐层 KV 和最终回答，依赖范围各不相同。固定 tokenizer 下的文档 token 可以脱离用户问题保存；双向编码器的文档 embedding 若由独立文档输入生成，也可在相同编码函数下复用。decoder 的第二段 KV 通常已经包含第一段的信息，不能仅用第二段文本定位一个通用的精确状态。

对因果 decoder，设输入为 A、B、Q，分别表示两个材料片段与问题。第一层投影的输入主要来自 token embedding、位置和该层前处理；经过 attention 后，B 的隐藏状态已吸收允许看到的 A。更深层 B 的 K/V 因而依赖 A。将 B 改到 C 后面，即使 B 的 token 完全相同、位置也碰巧相同，逐层状态仍可能改变。状态缓存身份应描述实际依赖，不能把文本哈希当作这些依赖成立的证明。

需要区分三个结果目标：完整函数的数值一致、在允许误差内的一致、任务质量达到阈值。选择性重算通常属于第三类；少数任务上的回答相同，不能升级为任意输入的精确复用。

## 精确复用需要满足依赖条件

已有完整前缀的 KV 可以在相同模型、adapter、token 序列、位置/窗口和数值格式下复用。若某模型明确规定片段间互不可见，独立片段的计算才有机会直接组合；这时参考函数本身必须采用相同可见性。人为关闭跨片段 attention 会改变原模型，不能作为原函数精确复用的实现技巧。

对于 RoPE，若旋转前向量确实相同，旧位置 p 的 K 可以通过 R(p′)R(p)ᵀ 转到位置 p′。这个等式修正的是旋转坐标；它不会重新生成因上文变化而改变的隐藏状态，也不会补回跨片段 attention。频率、缩放、旋转维度及其布局都必须相同。使用绝对位置 embedding、其他位置变换或依赖当前长度的缩放时，应重新建立对应的变换条件。

一个二维反例能检查实现是否保留了完整旋转。令旋转前 q=(1,0)、k=(0,1)，q 旋转 π/2、k 保持角度 0，则旋转后两者均为 (0,1)，点积为 1；只保留与 cos 对应的同维乘积会得到 0。相对位置不变性应由完整旋转矩阵验证。CacheBlend v1 附录的打印展开式省略了混合分量，本章使用矩阵恒等式推导，不依赖该展开式。

## 选择性重算如何连接缓存与当前输入

CacheBlend 的固定 v1 提出逐层融合：为一部分 token 重新计算当前层的 Q/K/V，将其 K/V 写入对应的逻辑位置，其余位置沿用缓存；被选择的 Q 与该层完整可见 K/V 做 attention，得到下一层需要的隐藏状态。被选择 token 的计算量下降，但全历史 K/V 的读取、装载和索引工作仍然存在。

选择集合必须来自在线可取得的信息。先完整计算一个早期探测区域，再比较新旧状态并逐步缩小重算集合，是一种可实施的路线。使用所有层完整重算得到的误差来选 token，属于离线 oracle，只能评价选择策略上限。具体在哪层观察偏差，要与真实计算顺序一致：若第一层投影尚未吸收上文，不能假定它已经暴露了深层跨片段偏差。

集合在逐层缩小时，下一层需要的 token 必须仍有合法输入隐藏状态；已丢弃 token 不能只凭一个新索引重新加入。允许重新扩张集合的实现，需要保留相应中间量或补算其依赖。查询文本、未命中的新片段以及必须产生最终输出的 token 应单独处理，不能被缓存命中比例掩盖。

这些规则保留了“部分更新”的可执行性，但不证明质量。高偏差 token 与最终回答的重要性并不总是一致：一个数值很小的否定词、跨材料的实体对应或少数位置的错误，也可能改变任务结果。重算比例应绑定模型、片段构造和任务分布；论文中的经验比例不能成为知识库默认保证。

## 多层缓存的状态与所有权

独立预计算的片段缓存与某次请求融合后的缓存是不同对象。融合结果依赖该请求的前序片段、顺序、位置和选择策略；将它覆盖回“独立片段 B”的公共条目，会污染后续请求。公共对象应保持其原始依赖含义，修改部分使用私有缓冲或写时复制；确需保存组合结果时，应登记组合依赖。

请求状态至少包含片段及版本序列、各片段的 token 范围、原位置与目标位置、每层就绪范围、重算选择集合、数值格式和当前代次。加载完成、位置变换完成、部分更新完成、消费者可见是不同事件。当前层只能读取已完成的数据；异步获取下一层时还需计入在途缓冲。取消后停止新工作，并等待已提交的读写结束再复用缓冲。

KV 量化、裁剪与片段融合的误差不能分别通过后直接视为组合通过。量化会改变偏差排序，裁剪会删除融合需要访问的位置，稀疏页布局也会改变 gather 的成本。近似缓存应沿用其构建策略身份，避免精确前缀路径误读它。

## 计算与传输要分别记账

设总材料长为 L，第 i 层重算 rᵢ 个 query。该层 attention 的逻辑工作与 rᵢL 相关，投影和 MLP 工作与 rᵢ 相关；加载缓存仍可能与 L 相关。选择、gather/scatter、位置变换、缓存解码、尾块浪费和不规则 kernel 的效率也都需要计入。因此“重算 10% token”等于“耗时 10%”仅是粗略候选模型。

对逐层加载与计算流水，设每层加载 a、计算 c，有 H 层且独立资源和足够缓冲，则理想时间为 a+c+(H−1)max(a,c)。设定 H=4、a=6 ms、c=2 ms，得到 26 ms，串行为 32 ms；若 c 增为 9 ms，流水为 42 ms，计算不能被 6 ms 的加载隐藏。实际还包括启动、尾部、选择和竞争开销。相同 PCIe、DRAM 或 HBM 被两阶段共用时，a、c 必须在并发条件下测量。

缓存容量也不是命中片段数乘一个常数。一个标准 KV 片段的有效字节为 2H L Hkv d s，此外有格式元数据、页尾、私有更新、位置转换和双缓冲。若多个组合必须分别缓存，复用率上升可能伴随容量急剧增加，需要比较保存独立片段后近似融合与保存少数常用完整前缀。

## 验证、反例与方案反转

先建立完整 prefill 参考，固定材料文本、顺序、问题、模型和采样设置。覆盖 A→B 与 C→B、A→B 与 B→A、同文本不同位置、一个字的否定修改、跨片段指代、不同 adapter、缺失缓存以及加载中断。记录逐层状态/最终 logits 偏差，同时在真实任务上测答案正确性、依据一致性和长材料表现。性能统计包含检索后到首输出的全部阶段；若声明用户端 TTFT，还须包含检索和重排。

精确前缀命中高、材料很短或设备重算很快时，常规前缀缓存与全量 prefill 更有利。长材料的非前缀复用高、传输可以与少量重算重叠且质量阈值允许时，选择性重算才可能获益。跨材料依赖强、查询分布变化或高精度答案要求提高时，应提高重算范围或回到完整函数。决定反转的信号是实际端到端成本与质量约束，而不是缓存命中率本身。

1. Introduction
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong
performance across a wide range of tasks (Brown et al.,
2020; Yuan et al., 2023; Chuang et al., 2023). However,
their deployment is very costly, requiring a large number of
hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Given these substan-
tial costs, one natural way to reduce the cost per request is to
combine a sufficient number of requests together for batch
processing. However, in this batch inference scenario, the
key-value cache (KV cache), which holds the attention keys
and values during generation to prevent re-computations, is
becoming the new memory and speed bottleneck. This bot-
tleneck becomes more pronounced with larger batch sizes
and longer context lengths. For instance, in 540B PaLM,
with a batch size of 512 and a context length of 2048, KV
cache alone can take 3TB. This is 3 times the size of the
model’s parameters (Pope et al., 2023). Also, the GPU
SRAM has to load the whole KV cache from the GPU de-
vice memory for every token generated, during which the
computational cores are idle. Thus, reducing KV cache size
in LLMs while maintaining accuracy is important.
Existing works towards this problem can be roughly divided
into three categories. First, some work suggests reducing
the number of heads in KV cache, such as multi-query
attention (Shazeer, 2019) and multi-group attention (Ainslie
et al., 2023). However, these methods require either training
the model from scratch or fine-tuning the existing model.
Second, another research line reduces KV cache size by
evicting unimportant tokens (Zhang et al., 2023). Third,
some other works try to solve this problem from the system
perspective, e.g., offloading KV cache (Sheng et al., 2023)
or extending virtual memory and paging techniques into the
attention mechanism (Kwon et al., 2023a).

namely, quantization. Unlike the well-studied weight quan-

our knowledge, only a few studies applied the vanilla 4bit

does not adversely impact the others.
Based on the above insights, we propose KIVI, a plug-and-
play extreme low-bit KV cache quantization method. KIVI
quantizes key cache per-channel and quantizes value cache
per-token. The per-token value cache quantization aligns
well with the streaming nature of auto-regressive inference,
allowing newly quantized tensors to be directly appended
to the existing quantized value cache by token dimension.
However, for per-channel key cache quantization, the quan-
tization process spans different tokens, which cannot be
directly implemented in this streaming setting. Since the
number of tokens in key cache can be arbitrary, our key
idea is to split key cache into two parts. The first part is
the grouped key cache, which contains several groups of
tokens and each group has a certain number of tokens. The
second part is the residual key cache, which does not have
a sufficient number of tokens to form a complete group.
Similarly, we split value cache into the grouped and residual
parts to maintain the model performance. We only apply
group-wise quantization to the grouped key cache and value
cache, while the residual key cache and value cache are kept
in full precision. The grouped and residual parts can be
combined when computing the attention score using tiled
matrix multiplication. Our contributions are summarized as
follows:
• Extensive analysis regarding the outlier patterns
and quantization error of KV cache in commonly-
used LLMs. Our observations suggest that key cache
should be quantized per-channel and value cache
should be quantized per-token. We also explain in-
depth why these caches require different quantization
approaches.
• A new plug-and-play 2bit KV cache quantization
algorithm without any fine-tuning, KIVI, with
hardware-friendly implementation. We conduct an
extensive evaluation for KIVIwith Llama (Llama-2),
Mistral, and Falcon on popular generation tasks. KIVI
can efficiently compress KV cache to 2bit and bring
2.6× peak memory usage reduction for Llama-2-7B,
with little to no accuracy drop. With our efficient
system implementation, this memory reduction in re-

2.35× ∼3.47× throughput.
2. Background: Attention Inference-Time
Workflow
The LLM attention inference-time workflow involves two
phases: i) the prefill phase, where the input prompt is used to
generate KV cache for each transformer layer of LLMs; and
ii) the decoding phase, where the model uses and updates
KV cache to generate the next token, one at a time.

where b is the batch size, lprompt is the length of the input

we ignore the layer index here. The key, value tensors can
be computed by
XK = XWK, XV = XWV ,
where WK, WV ∈Rd×d are the key and value layer weight,
respectively. After obtaining XK and XV , they are cached
in the memory for the ease of decoding.

Memory and Speed Analysis.
The above process is re-

tokens. From the above analysis, the shape of KV cache is
b × (lprompt + lgen) × d. To get a sense of the scale, consider

cache requires 1.2TB, which is 3.8 times the model weights
(Sheng et al., 2023). Besides the memory, the inference
speed is also decided by the KV cache size. The GPU needs
to load KV cache from GPU main memory to GPU SRAM
once for every token generated during which the computa-
tional core of the chip is essentially idle (Pope et al., 2023;
Kwon et al., 2023a).
3. Methodology
In scenarios with long contexts or batched inferences, the
memory and speed bottlenecks are storing and loading KV
cache size. The most simple and effective way to alleviate
this problem is to reduce the total bytes occupied by KV
cache, specifically, quantization. Following this motivation,
we first evaluate the performance of the existing quantiza-
tion method in Section 3.1. Our observations suggest that
key and value cache should be quantized along different
dimensions. We analyze the rationale behind this observa-
tion in Section 3.2. Then based on the analysis, we propose
KIVI, a new KV cache quantization method along with its
streaming data structure, detailed in Section 3.3.

3.3. KIVI: Algorithm and System Support
Algorithm.
As we previously analyzed, key cache should
be quantized per-channel and value cache should be quan-
tized per-token. Recall that key and value cache of newly
generated tokens arrive sequentially. From the implemen-
tation perspective, per-token quantization aligns well with
streaming settings, allowing newly quantized tensors to be
directly appended to the existing quantized value cache
by token dimension. However, for per-channel quantiza-
tion, the quantization process spans across different tokens,
which cannot be directly implemented in the streaming set-
ting. As shown in Figure 3, our key idea to solve this prob-
lem is to group key cache every G tokens and quantize them
separately. Because the number of tokens in XK can be ar-
bitrary, we split XK into two parts, namely, the grouped part
XKg = XK[: l −r] and residual part XKr = XK[l −r :],
where l is the number of tokens inside the current key cache
XK, r is the number of residual tokens, where l −r can be
divisible by G.
Since XKg can be evenly divided into (l −r)/G groups,
we only store Q(XKg) with group-wise quantization, while
XKr is kept in full precision. During the decoding process,
each newly arrived key cache tK is added to XKr and once
XKr reaches R tokens, which is a hyperparameter - residual
length, we quantize and concatenate it with the previously
quantized Q(XKG). Then we reset XKr to an empty tensor.
We note that R should be divisible by G. With tiled matrix
multiplication, the raw attention logits is then calculated as:
Ag = tQQ(X⊤
Kg),
XKr = Concat([XKr, tK]),
Ar = tQX⊤
Kr,
A = Concat([Ag, Ar]).
(3)
For value cache, similar to key cache, we also split it into
two parts and keep the most recent value cache in full pre-
cision, namely, XVg and XVr. Specifically, we maintain a
queue and each newly arrived value cache is pushed into
the queue. Once the queue reaches the predefined residual
length R, the most outdated value cache is poped. Then the
poped value cache is quantized per-token and concatenated
with the previously quantized value cache along the token
dimension.
As shown in Figure 3, we also emphasize that during the
prefill phase, the exact key and value tensors are passed to
the next layers, although only the quantized KV cache is
retained in memory. The whole algorithm can be found in
Appendix A Algorithm 1.

Analysis.
In KIVI, the grouped key cache XKg and value
cache XVg is quantized, while the residual key cache XKr
and value cache XVr is kept in full precision. By design,
there are at most R tokens inside XKr or XVr. In practice,
we set R ≤128 and the sequence length lprompt + lgen is
often much longer than R. Thus the memory overhead from
XKr and XVr is negligible when considering the benefit
from extreme low-bit quantization, especially for the long
context scenarios. Also, since the newly arrived key and
value tensors are added to XKr and XVr in full precision,
KIVImaintains a full precision KV cache sliding window
for the local relevant tokens. This window size is expected
to be R
2 for key cache, and R for value cache. Later in the
experiment section, we show that this full precision sliding
window is crucial for obtaining desirable performance on
hard tasks, such as GSM8K.
System Support.
We provide a hardware-friendly imple-
mentation for running KIVI on GPUs. To minimize the
overhead, we have fused the dequantization process with
matrix multiplication, e.g., Q_MatMul in Figure 3, using
CUDA. We also implement the group-wise quantization ker-
nel in Triton. Our method is fully compatible with weight-
only quantization.
4. Experiments
4.1. Settings
Models.
We evaluate KIVI using two popular recent
model families: Llama/Llama-2 (Touvron et al., 2023a;b)),
Falcon (Penedo et al., 2023) and Mistral (Jiang et al., 2023).
We note that the Llama and Mistral model is based on multi-
head attention, while Falcon is based on multi-query atten-
tion (Shazeer, 2019). We use the Hugging Face Transform-
ers codebase and implement the KIVIalgorithm based on
it. Following previous work (Sheng et al., 2023), the group
size G in Algorithm 1 for quantization is set as 32 across all
experiments, the residual length R for key and value cache
is set to 128.
Tasks.
As we analyzed in Section 2, the KV cache size
grows larger with longer context. Thus we evaluate KIVI
under the normal context length and long context setting,
respectively. Specifically, we adopt generation tasks from
LM-Eval (Gao et al., 2021) for normal context length eval-
uation and LongBench (Bai et al., 2023) for long context
evaluation, respectively1. For LM-eval, we adopt CoQA
(Exact match accuracy), TruthfulQA (BLEU score), and
GSM8K (Exact match accuracy). For LongBench, we chose

process with previous operations. We leave it as one of
the future work.

5. Related Work
Quantization techniques have been widely applied in Large
Language Models (Frantar et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2023;
Kim et al., 2023; Xu et al., 2023). A main branch of LLM
quantization is weight-only quantization, which involves
the quantization of model weights to lower precision. For
instance, AWQ (Lin et al., 2023) cleverly quantizes model
weights to INT4 and INT3 using an activation-aware manner.
GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022) utilizes approximate second-
order information to quantize model weights both accurately
and efficiently. SqueezeLLM (Kim et al., 2023) adopts the
concept of sensitivity-based non-uniform quantization along
with Dense-and-Sparse decomposition. This line of work is
orthogonal to ours, as they can be combined together.
SmoothQuant (Xiao et al., 2023a) is a post-training quan-
tization method that is more closely related to our work.
This method uses equivalent transformations to balance
the quantization complexity for both activation and weight,
making the activation easier to quantize. SmoothQuant can
compress KV cache to 8bit with minor performance loss.
However, it faces a significant accuracy drop when scaled
down to 4bit or less.
vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023b) and S3 (Jin et al., 2023) are
system-level works, which include memory management
through the use of PagedAttention or memory usage predic-
tion. These approaches can lower the memory requirements
of KV cache and simultaneously increase model throughput.
This research direction is orthogonal to our work, as such
system-level optimizations can also be applied to enhance
our algorithm.
Several other works also consider compressing KV cache
by evicting unimportant tokens. H2O (Zhang et al., 2023)
retains only a small portion of tokens that contribute signifi-
cantly to the attention scores. StreamingLLM (Xiao et al.,
2023b) is based on the observation of “attention sink” and
maintains only a few initial tokens to preserve performance.
Unlike these works, our KIVIretains all input tokens and
compresses them into lower precision. This line of work is
orthogonal to ours, as they also can be combined together.
6. Conclusion and Future Work
In this paper, we systematically analyze KV cache element
distribution in popular LLMs. We conclude that key cache
should be quantized per-channel and value cache should
be quantized per token. Based on these observations, we
propose KIVI, a plug-and-play 2bit KV cache quantization
algorithm without the need for any tuning. In real LLM
workload, KIVI allows up to 4× larger batch sizes and
3.47× throughput. In the future, we will further optimize
the implementation to reduce the overhead of quantization
process during the prefill and decoding phase.

Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs), despite their recent impressive accomplishments, are notably cost-
prohibitive to deploy, particularly for applications involving long-content generation, such as dialogue
systems and story writing. Often, a large amount of transient state information, referred to as the KV
cache, is stored in GPU memory in addition to model parameters, scaling linearly with the sequence
length and batch size. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach for implementing the KV cache which
significantly reduces its memory footprint. Our approach is based on the noteworthy observation that a
small portion of tokens contributes most of the value when computing attention scores. We call these
tokens Heavy Hitters (H2). Through a comprehensive investigation, we find that (i) the emergence of H2
is natural and strongly correlates with the frequent co-occurrence of tokens in the text, and (ii) removing
them results in significant performance degradation. Based on these insights, we propose Heavy Hitter
Oracle (H2O), a KV cache eviction policy that dynamically retains a balance of recent and H2 tokens. We
formulate the KV cache eviction as a dynamic submodular problem and prove (under mild assumptions)
a theoretical guarantee for our novel eviction algorithm which could help guide future work. We validate
the accuracy of our algorithm with OPT, LLaMA, and GPT-NeoX across a wide range of tasks. Our
implementation of H2O with 20% heavy hitters improves the throughput over three leading inference
systems DeepSpeed Zero-Inference, Hugging Face Accelerate, and FlexGen by up to 29×, 29×, and 3×
on OPT-6.7B and OPT-30B. With the same batch size, H2O can reduce the latency by up to 1.9×. The
code is available at https://github.com/FMInference/H2O.

Introduction
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in a wide range of natural language
processing applications such as content creation, summarization, and dialogue systems [1, 2, 3, 4]. However,
their deployment is very costly. In addition to the widely-studied bottlenecks of model size and the quadratic
cost of attention layers, the problem of the size of the KV cache, which stores the intermediate attention key
and values during generation to avoid re-computation, is becoming increasingly prominent [5]. For instance,
a 30 billion-parameter model with an input batch size of 128 and a sequence length of 1024 results in 180GB
of KV cache. A natural approach is to limit its maximum size as is done in classical software or hardware
caches [6]. However, it is challenging to reduce KV cache memory footprints in LLMs without accuracy drops.
While there exists substantial literature on sparse attention approximation in training, they have not
seen wide adoption for alleviating KV cache bottleneck. First, most existing methods, e.g., Reformer [7],
Flash Attention [8], and Performer [9], are designed to overcome the quadratic memory required by attention
mechanisms when modeling long sequences but still require a large cache size. Second, variants like sparse
transformers [10] or multi-query attention [11, 12, 5] can reduce the cache size, but directly applying them on

but their expensive eviction policies are difficult to deploy during generation.
Therefore, an ideal KV cache should have (i) a small cache size to reduce memory footprint, (ii) a low
miss rate to maintain the performance and long-content generation ability of LLMs, and (iii) a low-cost
eviction policy to reduce the wall-clock time during generation. However, there are three technical challenges.
First, it is not immediately clear whether the size of the KV cache can be restricted—each decoding step
might, in principle, require access to all previous attention keys and values. Second, identifying an optimal
eviction policy that maintains generation accuracy is a combinatorial problem1. Finally, even if an optimal
policy can be brute-forced, it is infeasible for deployment on real-world applications.
Fortunately, our preliminary exploration has yielded intriguing observations about the empirical properties
of LLMs. These findings pave the way for the potential design of an efficient KV cache.
Sparsity for small cache size: We observe that even when trained densely, the attention matrices of LLMs
are over 95% sparse at inference time (shown in Figure 2). This holds for a wide range of pre-trained LLMs.
Therefore, only 5% of the KV cache is sufficient for decoding the same output token at each generation step,
which suggests it may be possible to have up to a 20× reduction in KV cache size without an accuracy drop.
Heavy-Hitters for low miss rate: We discover that the accumulated attention scores of all tokens in
attention blocks adhere to a power-law distribution. It suggests that there exists a small set of influential
tokens that are critical during generation, named heavy-hitters (H2). H2 provides an opportunity to step
away from the combinatorial search problem and identify an eviction policy that maintains accuracy.
Greedy algorithm for low-cost policy: we surprisingly find that retaining the H2 based on local statistics at
each decoding step—summing the attention scores of only the preceding tokens—is as effective as considering
the attention of future tokens (shown in Figure 2).
Based on the above, we first rigorously define the generative process of LLMs operating with a size-
constrained KV cache in Section 2.1. Then we propose Heavy-Hitter Oracle (H2O), a framework that exploits
the properties of LLMs and uses simple, low-cost eviction policies that retrain the quality of LLMs throughout
the generation process. Specifically,
• In Section 3, we explore the emergence of H2 in attention, revealing their fundamental and critical roles:
(i) H2 exhibit a strong correlation of frequently co-occurring words in textual data; and (ii) removing H2
completely damages the model’s functionality. We demonstrate that H2 can largely lower the cache miss
rate of the existing policies mentioned above. Theoretically, assuming the attention scheme is submodular,
H2 corresponds to a greedy algorithm and is therefore near-optimal.
• In Section 4, we present a greedy but low-cost variant of H2 which is dynamically determined by the

2
Related Work and Problem Setting
Quantization, Pruning, Distillation for Inference.
To mitigate the resource cost of model inference,
various model compression algorithms have been investigated for decades. This big family roughly lies
into three groups: (1) quantization [19, 20, 21, 22]; (2) pruning or sparsity [23, 24, 25, 26]; (3) and
distillation [27, 28, 29, 30]. They pursue efficient inference from orthogonal perspectives and can also be
organically integrated. The techniques studied in this paper are closely related to sparsity but focus on a
different inference bottleneck, KV cache.
Sparse, Low-rank Attention Approx.
The quadratic computational complexity of attention modules
is one of the major bottlenecks of transformer inference [31]. Various efforts are devoted to addressing this
challenge like Reformer [7], Performer [9], Sparse Transformer [10], etc. The most relevant works that design
algorithms to reduce KV cache memory footprint, are considered as our baselines in this paper.
Caching.
Caching, which plays a pivotal role in optimizing system performance, entails the development of
effective eviction policies to handle frequently accessed data. Conventional approaches such as Least Recently
Used and Least Frequently Used [32, 33] prioritize the recency and frequency of data access. And the design
of KV cache encounters many similar challenges as traditional caching.
LLM Inference Breakdown.
The generative procedure of LLMs encompasses two distinct phases: (i) the
prompt phase, in which an input sequence is utilized to produce the KV cache (consisting of the key and
value embeddings), similar to the forward pass employed during LLM training; and (ii) the token generation
phase, which leverages and updates the KV cache to generate new tokens incrementally. Each generation step
relies on the previously generated tokens. The primary focus of this paper is to enhance the efficiency of the
KV cache in attention during the token generation phase, thereby accelerating LLM inference.

3
Observations
We present two key empirical insights of LLMs that inspire the design of H2O, as follows.
3.1
Sparsity for Small Cache Size
We first show an observation on the sparsity of attention in pre-trained LLMs. Then we discuss how it can
potentially unlock the possibility of reducing KV cache size without an accuracy drop. Given the normalized
attention score Softmax(QK⊤) matrix that is calculated by the query matrix Q and the key matrix K, we
set the threshold as one percent of the maximum value in each row and calculates the corresponding sparsity.
Observation.
We conduct zero-shot inference with the pre-trained OPT model on the validation set of
Wiki-Text-103. We plot the layer-wise sparsity within attention blocks and visualize the normalized attention
score matrix. The results are presented in Figure 2 (a). We observe that although the LLMs are densely
trained, the resulting attention score matrices are highly sparse, with a sparsity over 95% in almost all layers.
Insights.
The attention blocks’ sparsity suggests that access to all previous key and value embeddings is
unnecessary for generating the next token. This suggests it is possible to evict unessential KV embeddings
and reduce the requirement of KV cache during generation.
3.2
Heavy-Hitters for Low Miss Rate
The previous section showed the sparse nature of attention blocks in pre-trained LLMs, which provides the
opportunity for designing small KV cache size while still maintaining the performance of LLMs. However,
determining the best eviction policy that preserves generation accuracy presents a combinatorial challenge.
Although Belady’s Algorithm [34] is optimal and easy to compute for standard cache (offline), it is not
applicable for KV cache design. Because once evicting important KVs, it could destroy the performance of
LLMs due to the sequential dependency of LLM generation.
Observation.
Fortunately, in the early stage of our exploration, we find that the accumulated attention
scores of all the tokens within attention blocks follow a power-law distribution, as shown in Figure 2. This
suggests the existence of a small set of tokens that are critical during generation. We denote those tokens
as heavy-hitters (H2). In order to verify the importance of these tokens, we compare the quality of LLM

the accuracy drops drastically, confirming the importance of those tokens. Additionally, we can see the
accumulated attention score of each word (in red dots) have a high correlation with their co-occurrences in
the data (gray curve).
Analysis.
First, based on H2, we see an opportunity to side-step from the combinatorial search problem
and design a KV cache eviction policy that preserves the LLM generation quality. We conduct an empirical
study implementing a KV cache eviction policy that retains only the H2 and the recent KV embeddings in
the cache. The intuition is that recent words typically exhibit stronger correlations with current tokens. We
assess the effectiveness of this eviction policy through pre-trained OPT-30B and six downstream tasks. The
outcomes of these evaluations are illustrated in Figure 2. It is obvious that the H2 based eviction policy can
largely reduce the KV cache size without degrading the performance of OPT-30B.
Moreover, during the post analysis, inspired by [35], we find that H2 based policy is related to the classical
greedy algorithm (a polynomial-time algorithm with provable guarantees) under the assumption that the
attention schema is submodular. We present details in Appendix D.

4
Heavy-Hitter Oracle
The goal of this section is to propose the greedy algorithm using the H2-based policy and to show the
provable guarantees. We first present the H2-based policy called H2O cache eviction policy and formulate its
deployment in LLM generation as a variant of submodular maximization problem, named dynamic submodular.
Then we present H2O in the generative process, followed by a practical example of deploying our proposal.
Finally, we provide theoretical guarantees for H2O and show our efficient system implementation.

Implementation Details.
We provide a general framework that can support any KV cache eviction
algorithm and enhance throughput and reduce the latency of LLM generation with careful implementation.
For example, to ensure I/O efficiency, we do not swap memory when stored KV is evicted, but directly fill

5
Empirical Evaluation
In this section, our goal is to demonstrate that H2O, a remarkably simple KV cache eviction policy is capable
of enhancing end-to-end throughput and reducing latency in wall-clock while maintaining generation quality
across a broad spectrum of domains and tasks.
• In Section 5.1, we show that H2O can reduce the memory footprint of KV cache by up to 5× without
accuracy degradation on a wide range of model architectures (OPT, LLaMA, GPT-NeoX), sizes (from
6.7B to 175B) and evaluation benchmarks (HELM and lm-eval-harness). More importantly, can enhance
the performance of existing KV cache sparsification techniques.

Our experiments are based on three representative model families of LLMs, including the OPT [36]

variants of Sparse Transformers (strided and fixed) as strong baselines.

Conclusion and Discussion
In this paper, we study one of the key bottlenecks of LLM deployment, KV cache, particularly for long-content
and large-batch generation applications. We propose H2O, a simple KV cache eviction policy for significantly
reducing its memory footprint. The main insight of our approach is the recognition of a subset of tokens,
known as Heavy Hitters, which contribute the most value when computing attention scores. We formulate the
KV cache eviction as a dynamic submodular problem and provide the theoretical guarantees for our algorithm.
Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that H2O can significantly improve end-to-end throughput
and decrease latency in wall-clock time, without compromising the generation quality of LLMs across a
variety of tasks.

A
More Implementation Details
In this section, our goal is to provide the details of system implementation (mentioned in Section 4.2) and
experiment settings (mentioned in Section 5), as well as the pseudocode.
System Details.
We implement H2O on top of FlexGen. FlexGen is a white-box implementation of OPT
models, and we have done some surgery on handling the KV cache. Specifically, for the given parameter k, we
always maintain a list of KV cache with the first k entries as heavy hitters, and the last k entries as most
recent tokens. In order to avoid data movement in memory, the memory for KV cache is preallocated. We use
a circular queue to efficiently update the last k entries.
Experiment Details.
Our study involves the evaluation with varying sizes of KV cache that encompass
4%, 10%, 20%, and 60% of the prompt’s length. We select two tasks (XSUM and CNN/Daily Mail) from the
HELM framework [15] and present the performance based on 1000 test samples. Additionally, we employ
the lm-eval-harness framework [14] for six other tasks (COPA, MathQA, OpenBookQA, PiQA, RTE, and
Winogrande). For the tasks derived from the HELM framework, we report the performance for zero-shot
inference, while for the tasks from lm-eval-harness, we default to conduct five-shot inference.
Pseudocode.
We show some pseudocode to demonstrate our implementation skeleton. The function
generation_loop() is the base loop in FlexGen that controls prefetch and overlap the I/O streams and
computation. Then in function compute_layer(), the function attention_forward() will be called for
attention layers. The function compute_attention() will return new KV cache and the indices for evicted
entries during decoding iterations, which would be the place to implement a customized evict strategy. During
each decoding iteration, the oldest one among the last k tokens will be removed from the reserved last k
entries, one heavy hitter will be evicted for each head, and the newest token will be added to the KV cache
with a position in the last k entries. This happens in the function store_cache().

B
Extended Related Works, Discussions, and Limitations
The goal of this section is to first introduce more background and related works for Section 2, then describe
some previous attempts in our experiments as well as discuss the social impact and limitations of this work.
B.1
Extended Related Works
Efficient Inference of LLMs.
The substantial parameter counts of large language models (LLMs) present
significant challenges for inference. To overcome this limitation, previous efforts have employed model
compression techniques with specific designs to achieve efficient LLM inference, such as the method described
in [47], which employs one-shot pruning on LLMs (e.g., OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B), resulting in negligible
performance degradation even without retraining. Additionally, alternative approaches explore quantization
methods specifically tailored to LLMs, as discussed in [48, 49, 50, 51, 52]. These methods address efficient
inference from orthogonal perspectives and can be organically integrated. The techniques investigated in this
study are closely associated with pruning or sparsity but focus on a distinct inference bottleneck, namely,
KV cache. One closely related work[53] utilizes a learnable mechanism that determines necessary tokens
during inference but requires an extra fine-tuning process, which makes it less practical.
Quantization, Pruning, Distillation for Inference.
Previously, model compression algorithms have been
extensively investigated as a viable approach for mitigating the computational resource requirements of model
inference. These algorithms can be broadly categorized into three groups: (1) quantization [19, 20, 21, 22],
which involves mapping model parameters or activations from high-precision data types to low-precision
counterparts, such as using 8-bit integers instead of the commonly employed 32-bit floating point format;
(2) pruning or sparsity [23, 24, 25, 26], which aims to eliminate unnecessary neurons or weights within the
models; (3) and distillation [27, 28, 29, 30] where predictions from larger models are utilized as supervised
information to train smaller models.
Transformer in NLP.
Transformers [54] as a popular option have been frequently adopted by plenty of
natural language processing (NLP) applications with prevailing successes [55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 43, 60, 12, 61, 62].
Roughly, modern transformer-based networks can be categorized into two groups: (1) Encoder-Decoder or
Encoder-only (i.e., BERT-style models [63]). This type of transformers commonly leverages the Masked
Language Modeling task which encourages models to capture the intrinsic relationship between words and
their context. Notable examples include BERT [63], RoBBERTa [56] and T5 [64]. (2) Decoder-only (i.e.,
GPT-style models [65]). Usually, this group of transformers adopts the Casual Language Modeling task,
which is optimized to generate the next word/token in a sequence based on the preceding words/tokens. Such
an autoregressive manner is highly preferred by downstream tasks like text generation and question answering.
GPT-3 [66], OPT [36], PaLM [12], and BLOOM [67] are representative architectures within this huge family.
Training of Transformer.
Training a gigantic transformer-based model is not trivial. It notoriously
suffers from various issues such as overfitting, instability, etc. [68, 69, 70] analyze these bottlenecks from the
optimization perspective. To address the issues, a great amount of pioneering effort is devoted, including
data augmentations [71, 72], a better initialization [73, 70, 74, 75], customized optimizers [76], improved
normalization [77, 78], weight decay [79], and early stopping. However, there is still a long way to go before
we can fully clarify the mystery of transformer training.
19

Sparse, Low-rank Attention Approx.
The quadratic computational complexity of attention modules
is one of the major bottlenecks of transformer inference [31]. Various efforts are devoted to addressing this
challenge [7, 10, 9]. For example, Reformer [7] reduces the computational cost from quadratic to superlinear
complexity via locality-sensitive hashing. Performer [9] employs positive orthogonal random features to
approximate attention kernels. The most relevant work, Sparse Transformer [10], introduces sparsity to
reduce KV cache memory footprint and achieve an efficient attention mechanism, considered as our baseline
in this paper.
B.2
Discussions and Limitations
Previous Attempts.
During our experiments, we find several noteworthy observations. In H2O, employing
the accumulated attention score to evict KV embeddings can lead to a potential bias favoring the least recent
tokens. This bias arises because most previous tokens have a higher number of attention scores, resulting in a
higher accumulated attention score and, consequently, a greater likelihood of being retained. To address this
concern, we conducted an additional experiment utilizing the averaged attention score to determine which
KV embeddings should be retained. However, this alternative approach resulted in performance degradation.
Additionally, we observed a significant proportion of H2 occurrences at the beginning of sentences. This
finding suggests that the initial tokens play a substantial role in subsequent generation tasks.
Social Impact.
Our work represents an initial effort in designing a KV Cache policy, a realm that has been
relatively unexplored and yet is a significant bottleneck in LLMs. The proposed Heavy Hitter Oracle (H2O)
provide a solution to improve the efficiency of LLM generation, which can save energy cost and contribute to
green AI. Besides, our approach also serves as a sourc

C.5
Heavy-Hitter in MLP Blocks
Besides the attention blocks, the presence of Heavy-Hitters (H2) is observed within the MLP blocks of LLMs.
We utilize the Wiki-Text-103 dataset as the input and record the activated frequency of neurons in the
hidden layer of MLP blocks. As depicted in Figure 8, the activated frequency of neurons follows a power-law
distribution, wherein a small number of neurons are activated by nearly all input tokens (with a 100%
frequency) while the majority of other neurons are rarely activated.
Subsequently, a thorough examination of various characteristics pertaining to H2 in MLP blocks is
conducted, encompassing the following aspects: (1) The elimination of H2 leads to a substantial decline in
performance, although such degradation can be easily recovered even with a mere 1% of the training data;
(2) H2 exhibits a significant degree of overlap across different type of input content; (3) The emergence of
H2 occurs early in the training process, thus exhibiting an "early-bird" characteristic, and their positions
undergo gradual changes during subsequent training phases.
Elimination of H2.
We first train a GPT-2 using Wiki-Text-103 dataset and subsequently identify and
prune the neurons exhibiting an activation frequency exceeding 20% (i.e., H2). This pruning operation leads
to a substantial decline in performance, as evidenced by an increase in perplexity from 19.32 to 31.78. The
results emphasize the criticality of H2 in preserving the functionality of the model. To assess the recoverability
of the discarded information, we conduct a few-shot fine-tuning experiment, and the results are summarized
in Table 9. The pruned model is fine-tuned with varying ratios of training data for 500 iterations, and
it successfully regains performance levels equivalent to those of the pre-trained model. In contrast, when
training the model from scratch using only 1% of the training data, the resulting model achieves a perplexity
of 554.12 only. These findings demonstrate that the knowledge encoded in H2 can be easily restored.

CacheGen: Fast Context Loading for Language Model Applications
Yuhan Liu, Hanchen Li, Kuntai Du, Jiayi Yao, Yihua Cheng, Yuyang Huang, Shan Lu†,
Michael Maire, Henry Hoffmann, Ari Holtzman, Ganesh Ananthanarayanan†, Junchen Jiang

Abstract
As large language models (LLMs) take on more complex
tasks, their inputs incorporate longer contexts to respond to
questions that require domain knowledge or user-specific con-
versational histories. Yet, using long contexts poses a chal-
lenge for responsive LLM systems, as nothing can be gener-
ated until all the contexts are fetched to and processed by the
LLM. Existing systems optimize only the computation delay
in context processing (e.g., by caching intermediate key-value
features of the text context) but often cause longer network
delays in context fetching (e.g., key-value features consume
orders of magnitude larger bandwidth than the text context).
This paper presents CacheGen to minimize the delays in
fetching and processing contexts for LLMs. CacheGen re-
duces the bandwidth needed for transmitting long contexts’
key-value (KV) features through a novel encoder that com-
presses KV features into more compact bitstream represen-
tations. The encoder combines adaptive quantization with a
tailored arithmetic coder, taking advantage of the KV features’
distributional properties, such as locality across tokens. Fur-
thermore, CacheGen minimizes the total delay in fetching
and processing a context by using a controller that determines
when to load the context as compressed KV features or raw
text and picks the appropriate compression level if loaded as
KV features. We test CacheGen on three models of various
sizes and three datasets of different context lengths. Com-
pared to recent methods that handle long contexts, CacheGen
reduces bandwidth usage by 3.7-4.3× and the total delay in
fetching and processing contexts by 2.7-3× while maintain-
ing similar LLM performance on various tasks as loading the
text contexts.
1
Introduction
With their impressive generative capabilities, large language
models (LLMs) are widely used [1,5,7,11] in personal assis-
tance and recommendation, AI healthcare, and marketing, to
mention a few. The widespread use of public LLM APIs (e.g.,
GPT-4 [9]) and application frameworks (e.g., Langchain [10]),
combined with the open-source of industry-quality LLMs
(e.g., Llama [3]), further boosts LLMs’ popularity.
With LLMs increasingly used in complex tasks, many ap-
plications augment their user inputs (i.e., prompts) to LLMs
with long contexts containing at least thousands of tokens.
For example, some context supplements user prompts with
domain-knowledge texts so that LLMs can generate responses

This trend of long contexts is well reflected by the recent

short LLM inputs can still be useful [65, 92], many studies
have shown that longer inputs often help improve response

Although improving response-generation quality, using
long context poses challenges to response-generation latency,
as no response can be generated until all the contexts are
loaded and processed.
To tackle this latency challenge, previous work reduces
the computational delays of context processing by caching
the intermediate processing results: key-value (KV) features.
This way, instead of repeating the self-attention computation
on text context, whose complexity is super-linear to the text
length [25,39,87,98,113], LLM systems can directly use the
KV features and skip the redundant computation.
Unfortunately, previous work reduces the computational
delay at the cost of increased communication delay, as KV
features are multi-dimensional tensors of floating-point num-
bers and can be orders of magnitude larger than their corre-
sponding text contexts. The cost of loading KV features is
particularly concerning, as in practice, they often need to be
fetched remotely from another machine(s). For instance, a
database of background documents might reside in a sepa-
rate server and the supplementary documents assisting LLM
inference are only to be selected and fetched to the LLM

as the prompts from a user may spread in space (e.g., from
different locations) and time (e.g., two queries can be days
apart), they can be processed by different machines, so the
conversation history (i.e., context) must be loaded on-the-fly
to the GPUs serving the current request [2,13]. Some emer-
gent work shortens context, like dropping tensors, after KV
features are loaded into GPU memory [45,67,76]. However,
the dropped tensor information inevitably hurts LLM’s re-

large tensors, still require high bandwidth to transmit.
Therefore, solely optimizing computational delay is not
enough for long-context response generation and may even
degrade the end-to-end performance, as loading the KV fea-
tures increases the network delay. Instead, LLM systems must
optimize not only the computational delay but also the com-
munication (network) delay in handling long contexts.
This paper presents CacheGen, a fast context-loading mod-
ule for LLM systems, designed for (1) reducing the bandwidth
needed to transmit a context’s KV features and (2) minimiz-
ing the total delay in fetching and processing contexts, rather
than each separately.
CacheGen reduces the bandwidth needed for transmitting
long contexts’ KV features by compressing, instead of drop-
ping or rewriting, these feature tensors into more compact
bitstreams using a new KV encoder. The design of our KV
encoder leverages unique properties of KV features across
tokens and layers to achieve high size reduction and little
information loss. It uses a tailored arithmetic coder that takes
advantage of KV features’ distributional properties, such as
locality across tokens; it varies compression strategies across
layers of KV features, leveraging the fact that LLM’s gen-
eration performance has different sensitivities towards the
compression losses at different layers of KV features.
With its KV encoder, CacheGen has the flexibility of trans-
mitting a context in different forms, including KV features in
multiple bitstream representations each with a different com-
pression rate1 and the original raw text, which incurs more
LLM processing cost but no decompression cost or informa-
tion loss. Right before transmitting a context, CacheGen uses
a controller to decide which form to use, flexibly navigating
the tradeoffs among LLM generation quality, the transmission
bandwidth, and the decompression cost. It picks the context
form that optimizes the combined cost of transmission and
decompression, or the form that fits in a given time budget
with the least information loss.

cantly cuts the bandwidth usage for KV-feature transfers for
long contexts, thus outperforming the baselines that fetch
the KV features directly as well as the baseline that loads
the text context without the KV cache. For shorter contexts,

generation process includes two high-level steps. First, the
attention module processes the input tokens to obtain encoded
features. Then, the encoded features of the input are utilized to
generate new tokens in an autoregressive manner. Specifically,
the input tokens and previously generated tokens are fed into
the transformer model to generate the next token.
The key of the transformer architecture is the attention mod-
ule. Each layer of the attention module produces an attention
matrix, which models the connections between each pair of
tokens. The attention matrix at every layer is obtained by ap-
plying a non-linear neural network operation on the attention
matrix of its previous layer. Intuitively, the attention matrices
of deeper layers might embed a more complex understanding
of the tokens under consideration.
While the attention module is crucial, it is known to be
compute-intensive. Given an input of N tokens, the compu-
tation overhead of computing the attention matrices grows
quadratically, O(N2). Though the complexity could be re-
duced to O(NlogN) (e.g., [57,69]), such reduction often de-
grades the generation quality. Once the attention matrices are
obtained, the time to generate (decode) each token is quite
marginal and can be reduced to almost constant on GPUs.
2.2
Long contexts in LLM applications
Traditionally, the input of an LLM is a relatively short prompt,
as illustrated in Figure 3(a). Since the prompt contains limited
information, the LLM generates the response based solely on
the knowledge already embedded in the LLM itself.
However, as LLMs are used in more real-world applica-
tions, it is no longer sufficient to rely on the knowledge em-
bedded in the LLM. Instead, LLM applications often append
additional texts, referred to as the context, to supplement the
prompt input to an LLM3. To make our discussion more con-
crete, we highlight two types of applications, retrieval-based
apps and chat apps.
2“Tokens” in NLP stands for the input unit that is used for DNN inference,
which includes punctuations or splitting words into characters. Tokenizing
input is typically fast. We will use “tokens” in the rest of the paper.
3Since these contexts are often automatically added, users do not notice
or need to manually type them.
Retrieval-based apps (Figure 3b) use LLMs to answer
queries that require domain-specific knowledge. Examples
include question-answering systems [28,48,88], code under-
standing systems [61,88] or fact verification systems [48,61].
They use a background database that contains a large num-
ber of background documents. On retrieving a question, they
use embedding-based search algorithms (e.g., DPR [48,50],
BM25 [48, 85]) to quickly identify a subset of background
documents from the database, prepend these documents to
the prompt, and feed them together as input to the LLM. Note
that the search procedure is done by a seperate DNN or a
vector similarity search algorithm, which is not part of the
LLM.
Chat apps (Figure 3c) become popular with the rise of
OpenAI’s ChatGPT and have many similar products [8,37].
To produce high-quality and coherent responses, a user’s con-
versation history with the LLM, or at least part of it, is often
included in the input to the LLM as the context. For instance,
some applications supply a series of prompts to the LLM
(ChatGPT) to create a character in a video game and then
interact with the character by asking questions [56]. Chat app
users themselves are also intentionally using long prompts to
offer more background information (i.e., context) to the LLM.
For example, in few-shot learning, users provide several long
examples and their desired responses to the LLM before ask
the real questions [20,30].
Importantly, LLM applications use increasingly long con-
texts to raise the probability of including the right informa-
tion needed to generate high-quality, coherent responses. For
example, the user may ask “Which of the following coun-
tries generated the most total energy from solar sources in
2019?” [90]. It is hard for the LLM to answer the question
correctly without retrieving enough background documents
for the relevant countries the user is asking for. Though it is a
hypothetical example, many studies have shown that the accu-
racy of the generated answers increases with more retrieved
documents [48–50]. For instance, FiD [48] found that the
accuracy score increased from 40% to 48% when increasing
the number of context tokens from 1K to 10K. Retro [28]
shows that the perplexity (a proxy score of generation quality)
improves significantly when increasing the number of context
tokens from 6K to 24K.
3


=== PDF page 4 ===
To take in such long contexts, the LLM industry has been
training LLMs with the capability to accept ever longer in-
put sequences. For instance, Vicuna models [120], GPT-4-
32K [78], and MPT models [94] can take up to 32K tokens
as input. Latest models like LongNet [42] can even take up to
1 billion tokens as input.
In essence, long contexts play an increasingly important
role in LLM applications for two reasons. First, modern LLMs
have a superb ability to reason about new texts and potentially
learn new knowledge from them. To exploit this ability, many
works on in-context learning aim at optimizing what should
the LLM input encompass to induce better responses from
LLMs. Second, while LLMs are sometimes fine-tuned in
specific domains, it is not always feasible. For instance, it is
unrealistic to fine-tune an LLM for each user in chat apps.
The background database may be managed separately from
the LLM provider in retrieval-based apps. Due to their huge
number of parameters, fine-tuning LLMs is also slow and can
be very tricky to do right (e.g., catastrophic forgetting, loss of
reasoning ability, etc [43,64] ).
2.3 Saving computation by caching KV features
Recall that the computation overhead of the transformer (at-
tention module) on a context grows superlinearly (quadrat-
ically) with longer contexts (§2.1), so longer contexts will
dramatically increase the computation delay (Figure 4a).
Many recent works have tackled the long contexts’ com-
putation overheads. A common optimization, illustrated in
Figure 4b, is to cache the intermediate outcomes of contexts,
namely the key and value (KV) features, in GPU memory.
For a given text with N tokens, the KV features are two ten-
sors, each with the shape [N,c,l], where c is the number of
channels and l is the number of layers. For instance, with the
LLaMa-7B model, there are 4096 channels and 32 layers.
When the context is used again as part of another LLM in-
put, one can save the computation delay of processing the con-
text by using its KV features to reconstruct the self-attention
matrices of the context. To put it more concretely, the compu-
tation delay can be reduced by about 15-30× for the Llama-
7B model on contexts with more than 5K tokens, assuming
the KV features are already in GPU.
Caching KV features of a context, called a KV cache,4 can
be used in both chat apps and retrieval-based apps. In chat
apps, the context is the past prompts and responses, whose
KV features can be cached when the past prompts were first
processed and responses were first generated [38]. Retrieval-
based apps often preprocess each background document by
the LLM to compute the self-attention matrices and cache
their KV features [29,40,74,75].

3
Hidden network delays of loading contexts
Current LLM systems assume that the KV cache is already in
the GPU memory (or on the same machine), so they focus on
reducing computation delays. In practice, however, the KV
cache is not always in the memory of the GPUs that run the
LLM inference. Rather, the context of an LLM input often
needs to be fetched remotely from another machine(s).
In retrieval-based apps, the background documents can be
hosted on different servers than the LLMs [28,63]. One reason
is that background documents can be too big (even in raw
texts) to be stored locally on the GPU servers running the
LLM. For example, a recent work [63] uses a background
database that contains 364 Million documents [83], requiring
750 GB to store their texts. In another recent work [28], the
documents contain up to 2 trillion tokens and require 1 TB of
storage. Moreover, the background database may be managed
by a different service than the LLM service for proprietary
considerations [15,63].
In chat apps, a user may resume her conversation with the
LLM a few days after the last interaction. In these cases, the
KV cache of her conversation history may need to be swapped
out of GPU memory to save space for other active conver-
sation sessions [46, 112, 115]. Moreover, a user may issue
her prompts to the LLM from different locations at differ-

As KV features need to be fetched on-demand to the GPUs

to the end-to-end delay of loading and processing a context.
However, the size of a context’s KV cache can be orders of
magnitudes bigger than the context itself, making network
bandwidth a potential bottleneck. To put it in perspective,
for a context of 5K tokens, storing each token in int-8 repre-

by the Llama-7B model are two tensors, each with a size of
5K (tokens)×4096 (channels)×32 (layers), and the size of
